federal.verified: The withholding tables, rates and limits are the official amounts published by the IRS (Publication 15-T and Publication 15) and the Social Security Administration.
federal.notes: FUTA credit reduction for 2026: the final rates are published after November 10, 2026. Possible rates named by the Department of Labor: California up to 5.3% (at least 1.5%), U.S. Virgin Islands 4.8%. Enter the final rates in this window (credit reduction states) when they are announced. Pub 15-T 2026 Worksheet 1A (annual percentage method). Form W-4 from 2019 or earlier: $4,300 per allowance with the STANDARD schedules (married uses the married filing jointly schedule; single, and married withholding at the single rate, use the single schedule). Nonresident aliens: the Table 2 (2020 or later W-4) or Table 1 (earlier W-4) amount for the pay period (the annual amount divided by the pay periods, as printed) is added to regular wages for federal income tax only. Supplemental wages: 22%; the part of calendar-year supplemental wages over $1,000,000: 37% (also for exempt employees).

AK.name: Alaska

income.formula: No state individual income tax; no state wage withholding.

sui.agency: Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development, Employment Security Tax
sui.notes: Employees contribute 0.50% on the same $54,200 base (max $271.00 per employee per employer). Employer rate classes 1-20 = 1.00%, class 21 (delinquent) = 5.40%. New employer (industry) rate is 1.00% for every NAICS sector in 2026. Portions of UI contributions are statutorily directed to the STEP and TVEP training programs; these are not separate payroll lines. 2025: wage base $51,700, employee 0.50%. For 2027 the minimum employer rate may fall, and a new employer STEP tax was added to the law (AS 23.15.630). 2027 rates are not published yet: confirm them with the Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development.

AK.agencyUnemployment: Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development
AK.deposit: No state income tax withholding deposits. UI contributions (employer and employee) are paid quarterly with the quarterly contribution report, due the last day of the month after the quarter.
AK.notes: One of three states (with NJ and PA) with an employee UI contribution.

AL.name: Alabama

allowance.notes: Allowances = number of dependents (other than spouse) on Form A-4. Form A-4 exemption codes: '0' (no personal exemption), 'S' single ($1,500 personal exemption), 'MS' married filing separately ($1,500), 'M' married filing jointly ($3,000), 'H' head of family ($3,000). Dependents (other than spouse) are a deduction that depends on annualized gross income (GI): $1,000 each if GI <= $50,000; $500 each if $50,000 < GI <= $100,000; $300 each if GI > $100,000. If no A-4 is furnished, withhold using zero exemptions. Federal Form W-4 is not an acceptable substitute.

income.formula: 1) GI = wages per period x periods per year. 2) Subtract: (A) standard deduction from the income-dependent schedule for the A-4 status ('0' and 'S' use the single schedule); (B) annualized federal income tax withheld (this period's federal withholding x periods); (C) personal exemption ($0 for '0', $1,500 for 'S' or 'MS', $3,000 for 'M' or 'H'); (D) dependents x ($1,000 if GI <= 50,000; $500 if GI <= 100,000; $300 above). 3) Taxable = GI - (A+B+C+D), floor 0. 4) Tax: statuses 0/S/H/MS: 2% on first $500, 4% on next $2,500, 5% over $3,000; status M: 2% on first $1,000, 4% on next $5,000, 5% over $6,000. 5) Per-period withholding = annual tax / periods (may be rounded to nearest dollar). Bonuses and supplemental wages may be withheld at a flat 5%.
income.deviations: Standard deduction depends on annualized gross income and status (phase-down schedule); the employee's annualized FEDERAL income tax withholding is deducted before applying rates (so federal withholding must be computed first); the per-dependent deduction depends on gross income; personal exemption is a fixed amount by status, not per allowance.
income.localTaxes: Yes. Municipal/county occupational license taxes on gross wages earned in the jurisdiction (collected locally, not by the Alabama Department of Revenue), e.g. Birmingham 1%, Bessemer 1%, Gadsden 2%, Auburn 1%, Macon County 1%; Opelika 1% or 1.5% (confirm with the city). More than two dozen jurisdictions; rates generally 0.5% to 2%; based on work location.

sui.agency: Alabama Department of Workforce (formerly Alabama Department of Labor), Unemployment Compensation
sui.notes: 2026 rate notices use Schedule A: rates 0.14%-5.34% plus the 0.06% Employment Security Enhancement Assessment (ESA), 0.20%-5.40% in total. Statutory range across schedules A-D is 0.20%-6.80% inclusive of ESA, plus any shared cost. New employers pay 2.7% on first $8,000; ESA is 0% for new employers. Shared cost was 0.00% for 2025; confirm any 2026 shared cost on your rate notice from the Alabama Department of Workforce.

AL.deposit: Monthly (Form A-6, due the 15th of the following month) if more than $1,000 was withheld in either the first or second month of a quarter; otherwise quarterly with Form A-1 (due last day of month after quarter). Any single payment of $750 or more must be filed and paid electronically (My Alabama Taxes).
AL.quarterlyReport: UC-CR4 / UC-CR4A (Employer's Quarterly Contribution and Wage Report); withholding: Form A-1 quarterly return (A-6 monthly)
AL.annualReconciliation: Form A-3 (Annual Reconciliation of Alabama Income Tax Withheld) with W-2s, due January 31
AL.notes: Withholding booklet 'Withholding Tax Tables and Instructions for Employers and Withholding Agents', revised January 2026. Act 2025-334 (effective 2026): 30-day safe harbor - nonresident employees working in Alabama 30 or fewer days in a calendar year are not subject to Alabama withholding until the 31st day. 2025: same rates/brackets and formula (January 2025 booklet); SUI wage base $8,000, new employer 2.7%, Schedule A. No 2027 changes have been announced. Employment Security Enhancement Assessment (0.06%, experience-rated employers) is included in the total UI rate on the rate notice and is not a separate line.

AR.name: Arkansas

low_married.label: Low income tables elected - Married filing jointly

low_hoh.label: Low income tables elected - Head of household

allowance.notes: Personal tax credit of $29 per withholding exemption claimed on Form AR4EC, subtracted from annual gross tax. The regular formula does not vary by filing status; filing status matters only for the optional low-income tables.

income.stateForm: AR4EC (Employee's Withholding Exemption Certificate); AR4ECSP to claim exemption
income.formula: 1) Annual gross = period gross x periods (daily x 260). 2) NTI = annual gross - $2,470 standard deduction. 3) If NTI < $100,001 use NTI_used = floor(NTI/100)*100 + 50, else exact NTI. 4) Annual gross tax = NTI_used x rate - adjustment from the official table (Arkansas DFA table), rounded to nearest dollar; floor 0. 5) If employee elected low-income tables, subtract the low-income credit. 6) Subtract $29 x exemptions on AR4EC; floor 0. 7) Divide by periods. Supplemental wages (bonus, commission, overtime paid with regular wages) may be withheld at 3.7% flat.
income.deviations: The official method is 'rate x NTI minus adjustment' with a $50-midrange lookup for NTI under $100,001, annual tax rounding, and a sliding adjustment between $94,701 and $97,600 that makes high incomes pay 3.7% x NTI - $79.90. The marginal brackets listed reproduce the table to within about $1 per year up to $94,700 only; SerieX uses the official table for exact results. Optional low-income credit tables also exist.
income.localTaxes: none (residents of Texarkana, AR are exempt from Arkansas income tax; Texarkana, TX residents are exempt on wages earned in Texarkana, AR - Form AR-TX)

sui.agency: Arkansas Division of Workforce Services (DWS)
sui.notes: DWS 2026 figures: wage base $7,000; new employer 2.0%; experienced range 0.200%-5.100% with deficit levels of 6.100%, 8.100% and 10.100%; stabilization rate 0.200%. SB 560 (2025) reduced the base contribution rate from 1.9% to 1.8% and raised the administrative assessment from 0.1% to 0.2% effective 1/1/2026, so the 2.0% new employer rate = 1.8% + 0.2%. 2025: new employer 2.0% (1.9% + 0.1% admin assessment), range 0.200%-10.100%.

AR.agencyWithholding: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration
AR.deposit: New registrations are monthly filers: Form AR941M with payment due the 15th of the following month (zero voucher required). DFA reclassifies accounts to annual filing (Form AR941A due January 31) when deposits are under $1,000 for the period/year after notification. EFT required for certain larger filers (ATAP).
AR.quarterlyReport: DWS-ARK-209B (Employer's Quarterly Contribution and Wage Report)
AR.annualReconciliation: Form AR3MAR (Employer's Annual Reconciliation of Income Tax Withheld), due February 28; state W-2 copies with Form ARW3 due January 31
AR.notes: MID-YEAR CHANGE: HB 1001 (2026 fiscal session) cut the top rate from 3.9% to 3.7% retroactive to 1/1/2026; DFA posted the revised 'Formula Method Effective 01/01/2026' on May 29, 2026 (employer instructions revised 4/27/26). The tables shown are the current 3.7% tables. Employers are not required to recompute prior 2026 withholding. Standard deduction rose from $2,410 (2025) to $2,470 (2026). 2025: top 3.9%, std deduction $2,410, $29 credit. The DFA instructions do not say how to withhold when an employee files no AR4EC: confirm with the Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration. SerieX uses the revised 3.7% formula for all 2026 paychecks. Stabilization/admin assessment (0.2%) is included in the assigned UI rate.

AZ.name: Arizona

0.0.label: 0.0% of gross taxable wages (no Arizona tax liability expected)

2.0.label: 2.0% of gross taxable wages (default when no A-4)

allowance.notes: No allowances. Employee elects a percentage of gross taxable wages on Form A-4 and may add a flat extra dollar amount per paycheck.

income.formula: Arizona withholding per pay period = elected A-4 percentage x gross taxable wages for the period + any extra amount elected. 'Gross taxable wages' is the amount meeting the federal definition of wages (generally federal W-2 box 1 wages, i.e. after pre-tax 401(k)/section 125 deductions). Options: 0.5%, 1.0%, 1.5%, 2.0%, 2.5%, 3.0%, 3.5% (or 0% with certification). If a new employee does not complete Form A-4 within 5 days of hire, or does not renew a 0% election, withhold at the default 2.0%. No annualization, no brackets.
income.deviations: Not a bracket or allowance formula: a per-employee elected percentage of gross taxable wages is applied directly each period (plus optional extra dollar amount). The 2.5% individual income tax rate is not used in the withholding computation. No separate supplemental rate published: supplemental wages are withheld at the employee's elected percentage.

sui.agency: Arizona Department of Economic Security (DES), Unemployment Insurance Tax
sui.notes: 2026: positive-rated employers 0.03%-4.18%, negative-rated 4.41%-8.36%; new employer 2.0%. 2025: positive 0.04%-4.86%, negative 5.13%-9.72%, new 2.0%, wage base $8,000. Confirm your rate with the Arizona Department of Economic Security (DES).

programs.name: Job Training Tax
programs.notes: 0.1% of UI taxable wages (A.R.S. 23-769). Exempt: employers on the new employer rate, positive reserve ratio of 12% or more, negative reserve ratio, reimbursable employers; set 0 in State settings when exempt.

AZ.deposit: Based on average Arizona withholding over the prior 4 quarters: more than $1,500 per quarter - deposit on the same schedule as federal deposits (monthly, semi-weekly or next business day); $200-$1,500 - quarterly with Form A1-QRT; under $200 (and other criteria) - may pay annually with Form A1-APR.
AZ.quarterlyReport: UC-018 (Unemployment Tax and Wage Report); withholding: Form A1-QRT (Quarterly Withholding Tax Return), due April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31
AZ.annualReconciliation: Form A1-R (Withholding Reconciliation Tax Return) or Form A1-APR for annual payers, due January 31 with W-2s
AZ.notes: Withholding rules are unchanged from 2025 (the 2026 A-4 options did not change). Nonresidents working in Arizona fewer than 60 days in a calendar year are generally excluded from withholding (with related-entity conditions). Confirm your unemployment rate with the Arizona Department of Economic Security (DES).

CA.name: California

single.label: Single, dual income married or married with multiple employers

allowance.notes: Exemption allowance credit $168.30 per regular allowance (DE 4 line 1) per year (weekly $3.24, biweekly $6.47, semi-monthly $7.01, monthly $14.03). Separately, each ADDITIONAL allowance for estimated deductions reduces wages by $1,000 per year (weekly $19, biweekly $38, semi-monthly $42, monthly $83) before the standard deduction; estimated-deduction allowances must NOT be used for the credit. If no DE 4 is provided the employer must use Single with zero allowances.

income.formula: EDD Method B (exact calculation), applied per payroll period or annualized: 1) If gross wages <= low income exemption for status/allowances, withhold $0. 2) Subtract estimated-deduction allowances x $1,000/yr (if claimed on DE 4). 3) Subtract standard deduction ($5,706 single and married with 0-1 allowance; $11,412 married with 2+ allowances and head of household). 4) Apply the tax rate table for the status (single table also used for dual-income married/multiple employers). 5) Subtract exemption allowance credit = regular allowances x $168.30/yr. 6) Floor 0, de-annualize. Supplemental: 6.6% flat, or 10.23% for bonuses and stock options; or aggregate.
income.deviations: Low income exemption test on gross wages; married standard deduction depends on number of allowances (0-1 vs 2+); estimated-deduction allowances ($1,000 deduction each) are counted separately from regular allowances (credit $168.30 each), so deduction and credit do not use the same allowance count.

sui.agency: Employment Development Department (EDD)
sui.notes: 2026 UI rate schedule F+ (rates 1.5%-6.2%); new employers 3.4% for two to three years. California has an outstanding federal UI loan, so a FUTA credit reduction applies federally (enter it in the federal tax table when the rate is announced).

programs.name: State Disability Insurance
programs.notes: Includes Paid Family Leave; no taxable wage limit since 2024.

programs.name: Employment Training Tax
programs.notes: Employers with positive UI reserve accounts and new employers; negative-reserve employers generally do not pay (set 0 in State settings).

CA.deposit: PIT and SDI deposits follow the federal deposit schedule and accumulated PIT (2026 thresholds lowered from $500 to $400): accumulated PIT under $350 - quarterly (due 4/30, 7/31, 11/2/2026, 2/1/2027); $350 to $400 - monthly by the 15th of the following month; over $400 - next business day (federal next-day depositors) or semi-weekly (federal semi-weekly: Wed-Fri paydays due following Wednesday; Sat-Tue paydays due following Friday). Federal monthly/quarterly/annual depositors: under $350 quarterly, $350 or more monthly. UI and ETT are due quarterly. Electronic filing and payment (e-Services for Business) is mandatory.
CA.quarterlyReport: DE 9 (Quarterly Contribution Return and Report of Wages) and DE 9C (Quarterly Contribution Return and Report of Wages - Continuation)
CA.annualReconciliation: None separate - the fourth-quarter DE 9 reconciles the year; W-2s are not filed with EDD
CA.notes: 2025 Method B values (for corrections): standard deduction $5,540 / $11,080, exemption allowance credit $163.90 per allowance; 2025 SDI 1.2% no wage limit; UI wage base $7,000, new employer 3.4%. 2026 values come from the EDD '2026 California Withholding Schedules - Method B'. California does not conform to the federal no-tax-on-tips/overtime deductions. Supplemental wages (items marked supplemental, e.g. bonuses) are withheld at the 10.23% bonus/stock option rate; other supplemental wages (overtime, commissions paid separately) may use 6.6%.

CO.name: Colorado

married_filing_jointly.label: Married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse

allowance.notes: No per-allowance amounts. If the employee files a DR 0004, the dollar 'Annual Withholding Allowance' on DR 0004 line 2 (including zero) REPLACES the default amount; DR 0004 line 3 is an additional per-period withholding. Without DR 0004, the default amount is chosen from the federal W-4 Step 1(c) filing status: $11,000 married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse; $5,500 otherwise. No W-4 and no DR 0004: treat as single. Federal W-4 claiming exempt: generally withhold zero (see Wage Withholding Tax Guide).

income.stateForm: DR 0004 (Colorado Employee Withholding Certificate, optional); otherwise federal W-4 filing status
income.formula: DR 1098 (2026): 1a) taxable wages this period (including overtime); 1b) periods per year (1,2,4,12,24,26,52,260); 1c) annual wages = 1a x 1b. 2a) allowance = DR 0004 line 2 if provided (even zero), else $11,000 (MFJ/QSS per W-4 Step 1(c)) or $5,500 (all others; also when no W-4). 2b) max(0, 1c - 2a). 2c) x 4.40%. 2d) / 1b. 2e) + DR 0004 line 3 extra (or pre-2022 additional withholding request). Result 2f is the per-period withholding. Do not adjust Colorado withholding outside this calculation.
income.deviations: Fits the generic model (annualize, minus standard deduction, flat 4.4%) except that an employee DR 0004 line 2 dollar amount overrides the standard deduction for that employee.
income.localTaxes: Occupational Privilege Taxes (flat monthly 'head taxes', not percentage): Denver $5.75/month employee + $4.00/month employer (employee earning $500+ in Denver in the month; employer also $4.00 per owner/partner/manager); Glendale $5.00 employee + $5.00 employer ($750+/month); Greenwood Village $2.00 + $2.00 ($250+/month); Sheridan $3.00 + $3.00. Aurora repealed its OPT effective 1/1/2025.

sui.agency: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment (CDLE), Division of Unemployment Insurance
sui.notes: Rates are 'total combined' = base premium rate + support surcharge + solvency surcharge. 2026 introductory (new employer) rate, non-construction: 1.53% base + 0.17% support + 1.35% solvency = 3.05%; heavy construction 6.285%; political subdivisions 0.20%. 2026 combined range: positive-rated 0.72%-4.58%, negative-rated 5.895%-10.85% (0.006-0.008 schedule). 2025 wage base $27,200. 2027 (announced by CDLE): chargeable wage base $32,100 and the solvency surcharge is NOT in effect for 2027; 2027 schedule 0.008-0.011.

programs.name: Paid Family and Medical Leave Insurance
programs.notes: 0.88% total premium; employers with fewer than 10 employees owe no employer share (set 0 in State settings).

CO.agencyUnemployment: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment
CO.deposit: Based on annual Colorado withholding: less than $7,000 - quarterly (due last day of month after quarter); $7,000 to $50,000 - monthly (due 15th of following month); more than $50,000 - weekly (Saturday-Friday week, due 3rd business day after the Friday; EFT required). Form DR 1094 or EFT (EFT payment satisfies the return).
CO.quarterlyReport: UI premium and wage reports filed quarterly in MyUI Employer+ (formerly UITR-1 / UITR-1a); FAMLI quarterly wage report and premiums in My FAMLI+; withholding: DR 1094 (W-2 Wage Withholding Tax Return) per filing frequency
CO.annualReconciliation: DR 1093 (Annual Transmittal of State W-2 Forms), due January 31
CO.notes: 2026 formula updated for the federal OBBBA: default allowances rose from $5,000/$10,000 (2025) to $5,500/$11,000 (2026); rate 4.40% both years. Any TABOR-triggered temporary rate cut applies on the annual return, not to withholding. SerieX uses $5.00 for the Glendale employer occupational privilege tax (OPT); confirm the amount with the City of Glendale. UI support and solvency surcharges are included in the combined UI rate. Denver/Glendale/Greenwood Village/Sheridan occupational privilege taxes are flat monthly amounts (set up as local tax items).

CT.name: Connecticut

A.label: A - Married filing jointly, spouse employed (combined $24,000-$100,500) / married filing separately

C.label: C - Married filing jointly, spouse not employed / qualifying surviving spouse

E.label: E - No withholding (income at or below the exemption threshold)

none.label: No Form CT-W4 on file - flat 6.99%

allowance.notes: No allowances. CT-W4 withholding codes: A = married filing jointly with spouse employed and combined income $24,000-$100,500, or married filing separately over $12,000; B = head of household; C = married filing jointly with spouse not employed (or qualifying surviving spouse) over $24,000; D = no exemption/credit (MFJ both employed over $100,500, significant nonwage income, or nonresident with substantial other income); E = no withholding (income at or below exemption threshold or MSRRA); F = single. CT-W4 line 2 adds dollars per period; line 3 reduces. Employee who fails to give a completed CT-W4: withhold a flat 6.99% with no exemption.

income.formula: TPG-211 2026 Withholding Calculation Rules (unchanged from 2025): 1) annualized salary S = period wages x periods. 2) exemption from Table A for the code (based on S). 3) annualized taxable income = S - exemption; if <= 0, withholding = 0 (go to step 9). 4) initial tax from Table B for the code (A, D and F share one schedule; B and C have wider brackets). 5) + Table C 2% phase-out add-back (based on S). 6) + Table D recapture (based on S). 7) x (1.00 - Table E personal tax credit decimal based on S). 8) / periods. 9) + CT-W4 line 2 additional, or - CT-W4 line 3 reduction (result not below 0). No percentage method alternative. No CT-W4: flat 6.99% of wages. Supplemental pay with regular wages: compute on the total as one payment; paid separately: if tax was withheld from regular wages, tax on (regular + supplemental) minus tax on regular; if not, compute on the combined amount.
income.deviations: Exemption, 2% phase-out add-back, recapture and personal tax credit are all lookup tables driven by annualized SALARY (not taxable income) and the CT-W4 code; the credit is a percentage reduction of the tax, not a per-allowance amount. No standard deduction or allowances.

sui.agency: Connecticut Department of Labor (CTDOL), Unemployment Insurance Tax Division
sui.notes: 2026: wage base $27,000 (indexed); new employer 1.9% (down from 2.2%); charged rates 0.1%-10.0% divided by 1.125 for 2026 (max charged 8.9%) plus 1.0% fund solvency tax = contribution rates 1.1%-9.9%. 2025: base $26,100, new 2.2%, range 1.1%-8.9%. 2027: charged-rate divisor 1.053 (max charged 9.5%) per Public Act 21-200; 2027 wage base not yet announced.

programs.name: CT Paid Leave
programs.notes: 0.5% of wages up to the Social Security wage base; remitted to the CT Paid Leave Authority.

CT.deposit: Remitter class by liability in the 12-month look-back period ending June 30 of the prior year (for 2026: period ending June 30, 2025): over $10,000 - weekly remitter (paydays Wed-Fri due the following Wednesday; Sat-Tue due the Wednesday after the following week); over $2,000 up to $10,000 - monthly by the 15th of the following month; $2,000 or less - quarterly with Form CT-941 by the last day of the month after the quarter. Most new employers are quarterly. All returns and payments must be electronic (myconneCT).
CT.quarterlyReport: UC-2 (Employer Contribution Return) and UC-5A (Employee Quarterly Earnings Report) via ReEmployCT; withholding: CT-941 (Connecticut Quarterly Reconciliation of Withholding)
CT.annualReconciliation: CT-W3 (Connecticut Annual Reconciliation of Withholding) with W-2s, due January 31
CT.notes: TPG-211 (Rev. 12/25) states the 2026 rules and tables are unchanged from 2025, so the same tables serve 2025 corrections. Supplemental pay has no flat rate (aggregate method per IP 2026(1)). Fund solvency tax (1.0%) is included in the UI contribution rate. Supplemental pay: no flat rate (aggregate method), so supplemental wages are added to regular wages.

DC.name: District of Columbia

allowance.notes: D-4 withholding allowances (1 for self, 1 if head of household, 1 each for 65+/blind, 1 for spouse if filing jointly plus 65+/blind, 1 per dependent, plus additional allowances from itemized deductions). OTR Tax Notice 2022-08 tells employers to use the current DC rate schedule and 'the federal allowance amount' (IRS Pub 15-T allowance for 2019-or-earlier W-4s = $4,300 for 2022 and still $4,300 in the 2026 Pub 15-T). Some payroll software still uses $4,150 (2018 FR-230 value). If a DC resident employee does not furnish a D-4, withhold as if no allowances were claimed.

income.stateForm: D-4 (DC Withholding Allowance Certificate); D-4A for nonresidents (certificate of non-residence)
income.formula: 1) Annualize wages. 2) Subtract D-4 allowances x $4,300. 3) Apply the DC rate schedule (same for all filing statuses): 4% to $10,000; $400 + 6% over $10,000 to $40,000; $2,200 + 6.5% over $40,000 to $60,000; $3,500 + 8.5% over $60,000 to $250,000; $19,650 + 9.25% over $250,000 to $500,000; $42,775 + 9.75% over $500,000 to $1,000,000; $91,525 + 10.75% over $1,000,000. 4) De-annualize; add any additional amount from D-4. Supplemental wages: aggregate method (9 DCMR 139) - no flat rate. Lump-sum retirement distributions: 10.75%.
income.deviations: OTR has not published an updated FR-230 withholding table since 2018; employers follow OTR Tax Notice 2022-08 (rate schedule + federal allowance amount). There is no explicit standard deduction in the withholding computation. Only DC residents are subject (nonresidents working in DC are not taxed by DC).

sui.agency: Department of Employment Services (DOES), Office of Unemployment Compensation - Tax Division
sui.notes: 2026: Tax Table VI remains in effect (positive-rated 1.9%-4.4%, negative-rated 6.2%-7.4%); new employer 2.7% (the higher of 2.7% or the prior-year average rate); wage base $9,000. Plus 0.2% administrative funding assessment on the same base (max $18/employee). Unchanged from 2025.

programs.name: Administrative Funding Assessment
programs.notes: Payable in addition to the UI rate.

programs.name: Universal Paid Leave
programs.notes: Employer-paid only; no wage cap.

DC.deposit: Monthly/quarterly payers file Form FR-900Q quarterly (electronic on MyTax.DC.gov since tax year 2023); deposits due by the 20th of the month following the period per the assigned schedule. Annual filers (withholding threshold under $200 per year) file FR-900A (2026: deposit due January 20, 2027; return due January 31, 2027). Confirm your assigned payment schedule with the DC Office of Tax and Revenue (OTR).
DC.quarterlyReport: UC-30 (Employer's Quarterly Contribution and Wage Report, includes PFL); withholding: FR-900Q
DC.annualReconciliation: W-2s with Form WT (Transmittal for Tax Statements) due January 31; FR-900A for annual filers
DC.notes: The DC withholding instructions (Form FR-230) are out of date. SerieX uses $4,300 per allowance, as an OTR notice directs (some payroll software uses $4,150): confirm the amount with the DC Office of Tax and Revenue (OTR). Rate schedule unchanged since 2022, so the same values apply to 2025 corrections.

DE.name: Delaware

allowance.notes: $110 personal credit per exemption/allowance claimed, subtracted from annual computed tax. If no certificate is furnished, withhold as single with no allowances. Employers must send the Division a copy of any certificate claiming 14+ allowances or exempt status with wages expected above $168.50/week.

income.stateForm: Delaware Form W-4 (DE W-4); Employer's Guide also allows reliance on the employee's federal allowance count (pre-2020 W-4/W-4A) or SD/W-4A; W-4NR for nonresidents
income.formula: Division of Revenue annualized method (rate table 'Effective January 1, 2025', still current): 1) annual gross = period gross x periods (daily x 300, weekly x 52, biweekly x 26, semi-monthly x 24, monthly x 12). 2) subtract standard deduction: $3,250 single (and head of household) or married filing separately; $6,500 married filing jointly. 3) tax: $0-$2,000: 0%; $2,000-$5,000: 2.2% over 2,000; $5,000-$10,000: $66 + 3.9%; $10,000-$20,000: $261 + 4.8%; $20,000-$25,000: $741 + 5.2%; $25,000-$60,000: $1,001 + 5.55%; over $60,000: $2,943.50 + 6.6%. 4) subtract $110 x allowances. 5) divide by periods. Supplemental wages: no flat rate - with regular pay withhold on the total; paid separately: tax on annualized (regular + supplemental) minus tax on annualized regular.
income.localTaxes: City of Wilmington earned income (wage) tax 1.25% of gross earned income: residents on all earned income, nonresidents on income earned in the city; employer withholds and remits to the City of Wilmington. No other Delaware municipality has a wage tax.

sui.agency: Delaware Department of Labor, Division of Unemployment Insurance
sui.notes: 2026 Merit Rate Table (DOL): new employer 1.0%, new construction 1.0%, delinquent 6.3%, lowest 0.3%, highest 5.4%, wage base $14,500. HB 433 (2024): wage base $12,500 (2025), $14,500 (2026), $16,500 for 2027 and after; benefit-ratio experience method starts 2027 (benefit ratio + employer size add-on + industry add-on). 2025: base $12,500, new employer 1.2%. These are basic assessment rates; the 0.2% supplemental (operations and technology) assessment is billed in addition.

programs.name: Delaware Paid Leave
programs.notes: Employers with 25+ Delaware employees: 0.80% (up to 50% from the employee). 10-24 employees: parental leave only 0.32% (0.16% employee / 0.16% employer); 9 or fewer: exempt. Set the company rates in State settings.

programs.name: Supplemental Assessment
programs.notes: Operations and technology assessment billed in addition to the basic UI rate.

programs.name: Training Tax
programs.notes: 0.11% at the $14,500 base (confirm the rate on your 2026 Delaware Department of Labor rate notice).

DE.deposit: Frequency set by a July 1-June 30 lookback: $6,020 or less - quarterly (Form W-1Q, due last day of month after quarter); $6,020.01-$33,460 - monthly (Form W-1, due the 15th of following month); over $33,460 - eighth-monthly (Form W-1A, due within 3 business days after each period ending the 3rd, 7th, 11th, 15th, 19th, 22nd, 25th and last day of the month). New employers file monthly until the next lookback. Thresholds are from the Employer's Guide; confirm your schedule with the Delaware Division of Revenue.
DE.quarterlyReport: UC-8 (Quarterly Tax Report) and UC-8A (Quarterly Wage Report); Paid Leave wage/hours reports in Delaware LaborFirst; withholding W-1Q/W-1/W-1A
DE.annualReconciliation: Annual withholding reconciliation (Form W-3 per the Employer's Guide, section 3(g); the guide's section 21 references Form WTH-REC due January 31) with W-2s
DE.notes: Income tax withholding is unchanged for 2025 and 2026. Confirm with the Delaware Division of Revenue the filing-frequency thresholds and the reconciliation form name (the Employer's Guide may be out of date), and whether employees need a Delaware W-4 (the guide accepts federal allowances, but the Division also publishes a DE W-4). Confirm the 2026 training tax rate on your Delaware Department of Labor rate notice. The 2026 UI quarter-1 report deadline was extended to May 29, 2026 due to delayed UC-8 mailings (one-time). Daily payrolls are annualized with 300 days (Delaware annualized method: daily x 300).

FL.name: Florida

income.formula: No state individual income tax; no state wage withholding.

sui.agency: Florida Department of Revenue (Reemployment Tax)
sui.notes: Florida calls SUI 'reemployment tax'. Initial rate 2.7% until the employer has reported for 10 quarters; 2026 minimum 0.10% ($7/employee), maximum 5.4% ($378/employee). Unchanged from 2025. Benefits are administered by FloridaCommerce.

FL.deposit: No state income tax withholding. Reemployment tax is paid quarterly with Form RT-6, due the last day of the month after the quarter.
FL.quarterlyReport: RT-6 (Employer's Quarterly Report) with RT-6A continuation

GA.name: Georgia

married_filing_joint_one_income.label: Married filing joint, one spouse working

married_filing_joint_both_working.label: Married filing joint, both spouses working

allowance.notes: Dependent allowance $5,000 per dependent (and per additional allowance) claimed on Form G-4 (per period: weekly 96.15, biweekly 192.31, semi-monthly 208.33, monthly 416.67). If no G-4 is submitted, the employer may use the federal W-4 election if sufficient information is available; otherwise withhold as single with zero allowances.

income.stateForm: G-4 (State of Georgia Employee's Withholding Allowance Certificate)
income.formula: Percentage method (Employer's Withholding Tax Guide 2026, revised June 2026): 1) taxable wages for the period minus the per-period standard deduction for the G-4 marital status ($30,000/yr married filing joint with one spouse working; $15,000/yr single, head of household, married filing separate, or married filing joint with both spouses working). 2) minus dependent/additional allowances x $5,000/yr (per-period equivalents). 3) x 4.99%. 4) If zero allowances claimed, subtract the standard deduction only. Annualized equivalent: (annual wages - std ded - 5,000 x allowances) x 4.99% / periods. Bonuses and other compensation: withheld at the income tax rate in effect when paid (4.99% from May 11, 2026; 5.19% before).
income.localTaxes: none (Georgia law prohibits local income taxes)

sui.agency: Georgia Department of Labor (GDOL)
sui.notes: 2026: wage base $9,500; experience range 0.04%-8.1%. New employer total 2.70% = 2.64% UI contribution rate + 0.06% administrative assessment. Some guidance says the 0.06% assessment applies only to experience-rated employers (not to minimum or maximum rate, reimbursing, nonprofit or new employers): confirm your total rate with the Georgia Department of Labor (GDOL). SB 160: 2.64% new-employer rate and the 0.06% assessment are in effect through December 31, 2026; from January 1, 2027 the new employer rate returns to 2.7% and the assessment expires (unless extended). 2025: same values.

GA.deposit: Semi-weekly (EFT) if more than $50,000 withheld in the 12-month lookback period ending the prior June 30 (Wed/Thu/Fri paydays due following Wednesday; Sat-Tue paydays due following Friday); monthly if more than $200 per month (payment by the 15th of the following month); quarterly if $200 per month or less but more than $800 per year (with Form G-7 by the last day of the month after the quarter); annual if $800 or less per year (by request). Form G-7 quarterly return required for all. Payments over $500 must be made electronically.
GA.quarterlyReport: DOL-4N (Employer's Quarterly Tax and Wage Report); withholding: Form G-7 quarterly return (2026 due dates 4/30, 7/31, 11/2/2026, 2/1/2027)
GA.annualReconciliation: Form G-1003 (Income Statement Transmittal) with W-2s/1099-NEC, due February 1, 2027 for 2026
GA.notes: MID-YEAR CHANGE: HB 463 (signed May 11, 2026) cut the rate from 5.19% to 4.99% retroactive to 1/1/2026 and raised the standard deduction ($15,000/$30,000) and dependent deduction ($5,000). Withholding: 5.19% rules before May 11, 2026; 4.99% rules on/after. 2025: 5.19%, $12,000/$24,000, $4,000 per dependent. 2027: HB 463 schedules further annual rate reductions toward 3.99% (0.125 point per year); 2027 tables not yet published. HB 463 also creates Georgia subtractions for qualified overtime and cash tips (up to $1,750 each, 2026-2028) reported on W-2 Box 14/G-1003 for 2026; they do not change 2026 withholding. Georgia does not conform to the federal tips/overtime exclusions. SerieX uses the 4.99% rules (June 2026 guide) for all 2026 paychecks. UI administrative assessment (0.06%) is included in the 2.70% new employer rate.

HI.name: Hawaii

single.label: Single or unmarried head of household

allowance.notes: $1,144 per HW-4 allowance per year (weekly $22.00). Head of household is treated as single. No HW-4 furnished: withhold as single with zero allowances. Federal Form W-4 may not be used.

income.stateForm: HW-4 (Employee's Withholding Allowance and Status Certificate)
income.formula: Booklet A annualized method (withholding on wages paid on/after January 1, 2026): 1) annual wages = period wages x periods. 2) subtract HW-4 allowances x $1,144. 3) subtract the extra lump sum withholding allowance $4,350 (every employee). 4) apply the single (incl. unmarried head of household) or married rate table. 5) divide by periods. Do not withhold amounts under 10 cents. Supplemental wages: paid with regular wages - withhold on the aggregate; paid separately - aggregate with the current or last regular wages and subtract tax already withheld (no flat supplemental rate).

sui.agency: Hawaii Department of Labor and Industrial Relations (DLIR), Unemployment Insurance Division
sui.notes: 2026 contribution rate Schedule C (0.0%-5.6%); new employers 2.4%; wage base $64,500. 2025: Schedule C, base $62,000, new 2.4%. DLIR forecasts a lower schedule for 2027 (not yet published).

programs.name: Temporary Disability Insurance
programs.notes: Employee share up to 0.5% of weekly wages, capped at $7.50 per week (2026; maximum weekly wage base $1,500.21). The weekly cap is applied to each paycheck times the weeks in its pay period.

programs.name: Employment and Training Assessment
programs.notes: Employers whose UI rate is above zero and below the schedule maximum.

HI.agencyUnemployment: Hawaii Department of Labor and Industrial Relations
HI.deposit: Annual withholding liability $5,000 or less: quarterly (Form VP-1 by the 15th of the month after the quarter); over $5,000 up to $40,000: monthly (VP-1 by the 15th of the following month); over $40,000, or federal semi-weekly depositor: semi-weekly (federal timing, EFT). Employers over $40,000 must e-file HW-14 and HW-2.
HI.quarterlyReport: UC-B6 (Quarterly Wage, Contribution and Employment and Training Assessment Report); withholding: HW-14 (Withholding Tax Return), filed quarterly
HI.annualReconciliation: HW-30 (Employer's Annual Transmittal of Hawaii Income Tax Withheld from Wages) with HW-2/W-2 copies, due January 31 (not needed when EFW2 is uploaded online)
HI.notes: Booklet A (Rev. 2025), effective December 5, 2025 for withholding January 1, 2026 and after. Only change from 2025 withholding: extra lump sum allowance rose from $1,650 (2025) to $4,350 (2026); $1,144 allowance and rate tables unchanged. Act 46 (2024) bracket widening applies on the annual N-11 return, not to these withholding tables.

IA.name: Iowa

A_other_or_mfj_spouse_has_income.label: Other (single, or MFJ whose spouse has earned income)

C_mfj_spouse_no_income_or_qualifying_sur.label: MFJ, spouse has no earned income, or qualifying surviving spouse

allowance.notes: Allowances = IA W-4 total allowance dollar amount / $40 (2024+ form) or the allowance count (2023 or earlier form). For a 2024-or-later IA W-4 the employee reports a TOTAL ALLOWANCE DOLLAR AMOUNT (W) that is used directly as an annual credit (each allowance on the form worksheet is worth $40). For an IA W-4 dated 2023 or earlier, W = number of allowances x $40. Per period, subtract W / pay periods from the tax.

income.formula: Iowa Withholding Formula effective Jan 1, 2026 (released Nov 2025): T1 = G - D (G = gross taxable wages for the period after pre-tax retirement/health deductions; D = per-period deduction: column A $13,000/yr [weekly $250, biweekly $500, semimonthly $541.67, monthly $1,083.33, daily $50] for 'Other', missing status, or MFJ whose spouse has earned income; column B $19,500/yr for head of household; column C $26,000/yr for MFJ whose spouse has no earned income, or qualifying surviving spouse; legacy 2023-or-earlier forms: Single $13,000, Married $26,000). T2 = T1 x 3.80%. T3 = T2 - (W / P) where W = allowance dollar amount (2024+ form) or allowances x $40 (2023-or-earlier form) and P = pay periods (daily 260, weekly 52, biweekly 26, semimonthly 24, monthly 12, annual 1). T4 = T3 + additional amount requested. Other pay frequencies: annualize, compute T3, divide by periods, add additional amount.
income.deviations: Fits the generic model (annual standard deduction by status, flat 3.8%, credit per allowance). For 2024+ IA W-4s the credit input is a dollar amount rather than a count. The official text does not state a floor; treat a negative T1 or T3 as zero.
income.localTaxes: none withheld by employers (Iowa school district / EMS surtaxes are paid with the individual return, not through payroll withholding)

sui.agency: Iowa Workforce Development (IWD)
sui.notes: SF 607 (signed June 6, 2025) cut the wage base from two-thirds to one-third of the prior-year average annual wage and lowered the maximum rate from 9% to 5.4% starting 2026. Rate Table D (lowest) applies for 2026. New non-construction employers get the rank-4 rate of the table in effect with a 1.000% floor (Table D rank 4 = 0.300%, so 1.000%); new construction employers 5.4%. 2025 wage base was $39,500. Table D is expected again for 2027; confirm with Iowa Workforce Development (IWD).

IA.deposit: Iowa DOR assigns semimonthly (1st-15th due the 25th; 16th-end due the 10th of the next month; six deposits per quarter), monthly, or quarterly deposit schedules, with a quarterly return due the last day of the month after each quarter. Usual thresholds: quarterly under $6,000 a year, monthly $6,000-$120,000 a year, semimonthly over $120,000 a year; confirm your schedule with the Iowa Department of Revenue.
IA.quarterlyReport: Iowa withholding quarterly return (GovConnectIowa); IWD Employer's Contribution and Payroll Report (quarterly, via My Iowa UI)
IA.annualReconciliation: VSP (Verified Summary of Payments Report) with W-2/1099 data, due January 31
IA.notes: The Iowa withholding formula has no separate supplemental flat rate, so SerieX adds supplemental wages to regular wages. A flat 3.8% is often used when the federal flat-rate method is used: confirm with the Iowa Department of Revenue before using it. 2025 withholding also used a flat 3.8% rate, with different deduction amounts.

ID.name: Idaho

married_withhold_at_single_rate.label: Married, but withhold at single rate

allowance.notes: ID W-4 allowances are multiplied by the Idaho Child Tax Credit Allowance Table (ICTCAT) amount, which is now ZERO because the Idaho child tax credit sunset (Idaho Code 63-3029L). Before the July 2026 table update the allowance was $3,868 per allowance per year. Single table also covers head of household and 'married, but withhold at single rate'. No ID W-4: withhold as single with zero allowances.

income.formula: Annualized wage method (Table for Percentage Computation Method EPB00744, 07-23-2026): 1) annual wages = period wages x periods. 2) subtract allowances x ICTCAT amount (currently $0). 3) tax = 5.3% of the amount over $16,100 (single, head of household, married-withhold-at-single) or over $32,200 (married). 4) divide by periods; add any additional amount from ID W-4. Supplemental wages: add to regular wages and treat as one payment, or withhold a flat 5.3% on a separately issued payment.

sui.agency: Idaho Department of Labor (IDOL), Unemployment Insurance Tax
sui.notes: 2026 (Administrative Order 682): wage base $58,300 (2025: $55,300); no reserve tax; standard (new employer) rate 1.000% = 0.97000% UI + 0.03000% workforce development + 0.00000% administrative reserve. Positive classes 0.208%-0.694%, deficit classes 1.25%-5.4%. All tax rates include the workforce development rate; no administrative reserve rate in effect for 2026.

ID.deposit: Form 910 filing cycle assigned by the Tax Commission: semimonthly if withholding is at least $25,000 per month or $300,000 per 12 months (due the 20th for days 1-15 and the 5th of the next month for the 16th-end); monthly if under $25,000 per month and more than $750 per quarter, or only one monthly pay period (due the 20th of the following month); quarterly if $750 or less per quarter (due last day of month after quarter); annual for certain small/agricultural employers (due January 31). Payments of $100,000 or more must be electronic. A zero Form 910 is required for periods with no withholding.
ID.quarterlyReport: TAX020 (Employer Quarterly Unemployment Insurance Tax Report); withholding: Form 910 per filing cycle
ID.annualReconciliation: Form 967 (Idaho Annual Withholding Report) with state W-2 copies, due January 31
ID.notes: MID-YEAR CHANGE: the Tax Commission revised the withholding tables (dated July 23, 2026; announced July 31, 2026) for the sunset of the Idaho child tax credit: thresholds now $16,100/$32,200 (previously $15,000/$30,000) and allowance value $0 (previously $3,868). Employers apply the new tables going forward and need not adjust withholding back to January 1. 2025: 5.3% (HB 40 cut from 5.695%, tables effective May 1, 2025), thresholds $15,000/$30,000, allowance $3,868. SerieX uses the July 23, 2026 tables (allowance $0, thresholds $16,100/$32,200) for all 2026 paychecks. Workforce development rate is included in every assigned UI rate.

IL.name: Illinois

allowance.notes: IL-W-4 Line 1 allowances (basic allowances: employee, spouse, dependents) are worth $2,925 each per year in 2026 (was $2,850 in 2025). IL-W-4 Line 2 allowances (additional allowances for age 65+ / legally blind employee or spouse) are worth $1,000 each per year. Both are subtracted from wages before applying 4.95%.

income.formula: Automated payroll method (Booklet IL-700-T, 2026): 1) wages for the pay period; 2) exemptions = ((Line 1 allowances x $2,925) + (Line 2 allowances x $1,000)) / number of pay periods in the year; 3) taxable = wages - exemptions (not below 0); 4) tax = taxable x 0.0495; 5) add IL-W-4 Line 3 additional amount. Example in booklet: $800 weekly, 2 Line-1 + 2 Line-2 allowances -> (800 - 7,850/52) x 0.0495 = $32.13.
income.deviations: Two allowance types with different annual values ($2,925 for IL-W-4 Line 1, $1,000 for Line 2). With Line 1 allowances only, the generic model (no standard deduction, flat 4.95%, deductionPerAllowance 2,925) reproduces the official method exactly. Per-period computation is mathematically identical to annualize/de-annualize.
income.localTaxes: none (no local income or wage taxes withheld by employers)

sui.agency: Illinois Department of Employment Security (IDES)
sui.notes: 2026 standard (new/ineligible employer) rate 3.350%; new employers in NAICS sector 56 (Administrative & Support & Waste Management) 3.450%. All IDES rates include the 0.550% fund building rate. State experience factor 102%. Small employer rate option 5.4% (gross wages under $50,000). 2025 values: wage base $13,916, standard rate 3.650% (NAICS 56: 3.750%), min 0.750%, max 7.850%.

IL.deposit: Schedule set by look-back period (12 months ending June 30 of the prior year; for 2026: July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025). Monthly (due the 15th of the following month) if $12,000 or less was withheld in the look-back period (and for new employers); semi-weekly (Wednesday/Friday federal-style schedule, electronic payment required) if more than $12,000 in the look-back period or more than $12,000 in any quarter (switch applies from the next quarter). Payments via Form IL-501 / MyTax Illinois.
IL.quarterlyReport: Form IL-941, Illinois Withholding Income Tax Return (quarterly); IDES Form UI-3/40, Employer's Contribution and Wage Report (quarterly)
IL.annualReconciliation: None. Illinois has no annual withholding reconciliation return; W-2 data must be filed electronically with IDOR by January 31.
IL.notes: Supplemental wages: 4.95% (Illinois' single flat rate). The booklet has no separate supplemental method: confirm with the Illinois Department of Revenue how exemptions apply to bonuses paid separately. 2027 values are not announced yet. Confirm the quarterly unemployment report form (UI-3/40) with the Illinois Department of Employment Security (IDES).

IN.name: Indiana

allowance.notes: Form WH-4: line 5 personal exemptions (self, spouse, plus extra exemptions for age 65+/blind) $1,000 each per year (Table A); line 6 additional dependent exemptions $1,500 each (Table B); line 7 first-time additional dependent exemptions $1,500 each (Table B); line 8 adopted child dependent exemptions $3,000 each (Table C). All are subtracted from wages before computing BOTH state and county tax.

income.formula: Departmental Notice #1 (effective Jan 1, 2026): 1) per-period deduction constant = ($1,000 x WH-4 line 5 + $1,500 x line 6 + $1,500 x line 7 + $3,000 x line 8) / pay periods per year (DOR publishes rounded constants: e.g. weekly $19.23 per personal exemption, $28.85 per dependent, $57.69 per adopted child); 2) taxable = gross wages - deduction constant; 3) state tax = taxable x 0.0295; 4) county tax = taxable x county rate (county of residence on January 1; if the employee lived outside Indiana on January 1, the county of principal employment on January 1); 5) add any additional amount requested. For one-time or non-periodic payments such as a bonus check, compute withholding WITHOUT exemptions. Indiana does not follow the federal no-withholding allowance under IRC 3402(n).
income.deviations: Multiple exemption types with different values ($1,000 / $1,500 / $3,000) and a county income tax computed on the same taxable base. With personal exemptions only, the state portion fits the generic model (flat 2.95%, deductionPerAllowance 1,000). Supplemental/bonus checks: no exemptions.
income.localTaxes: County income tax (Indiana Local Income Tax) withheld with state tax on the same taxable wages; rate set by county of residence on January 1 (nonresidents of Indiana on January 1: county of principal work on January 1). 2026 rates range 0.5% (Porter) to 3.0% (Randolph); SerieX includes every county rate. Employees working in Indiana 30 days or less may be exempt from state and county withholding under the nonresident 30-day rule (WH-4AFF).

sui.agency: Indiana Department of Workforce Development (DWD)
sui.notes: Most new employers pay 2.5% for their first four calendar years. DWD lists construction new employers as '2.5%, the lesser of 4.0 or the average rate for all construction companies'; government 1.6% unless reimbursing; successors inherit predecessor rate. Maximum 7.4% for employers in good standing, 9.4% delinquent maximum. Rates are determined as of June 30 for the next calendar year.

IN.deposit: DOR assigns an annual, quarterly, monthly or early-filer (larger withholders) schedule based on average monthly withholding; Form WH-1 is filed and paid electronically through INTIME for every assigned period, even with zero withholding. Monthly and quarterly returns are usually due by the end of the month after the period, and early filers by the 20th; confirm your thresholds and due dates with the Indiana Department of Revenue.
IN.quarterlyReport: Form WH-1, Indiana Withholding Tax Voucher/Return (per assigned frequency, via INTIME); DWD UC-1 Quarterly Contribution Report and UC-5A Quarterly Wage Report (filed in Uplink)
IN.annualReconciliation: Form WH-3, Annual Withholding Tax Reconciliation, with W-2/1099 data, due January 31 (electronic if more than 25 statements)
IN.notes: County rates come from Departmental Notice #1 (revision R46, 01-26). Counties may change rates effective October 1 and the Indiana Department of Revenue then republishes the notice, so check county rates from time to time. State rate: 3.0% for 2025, 2.95% for 2026, scheduled 2.90% for 2027. Confirm deposit thresholds with the Indiana Department of Revenue, and the UC-1 / UC-5A unemployment forms with the Indiana Department of Workforce Development (DWD). County income tax is withheld as a local tax item at the county rate, on wages after the same WH-4 exemptions (as Departmental Notice #1 describes).

KS.name: Kansas

allowance.notes: K-4 line 4 gives a total allowance count; line 3 gives the allowance rate (Single or Joint). Annual allowance amount = for the Single rate: first allowance $9,160, each additional allowance $2,320; for the Joint rate: first two allowances $9,160 each, each additional allowance $2,320 (head of household and dependents use $2,320 allowances). These amounts match the KW-100 wage-bracket tables. Divide by pay periods.

income.formula: KW-100 percentage formula (wages paid on/after July 1, 2024; still current for 2026): 1) allowance amount = (Single: 9,160 x min(n,1) + 2,320 x max(n-1,0); Joint: 9,160 x min(n,2) + 2,320 x max(n-2,0)) / pay periods; 2) net wages = gross wages - allowance amount; 3) apply period table. Annual tables: Single (incl. head of household): $0-$3,605 = 0; $3,605-$26,605 = 5.2% of excess over $3,605; over $26,605 = $1,196.00 + 5.58% of excess over $26,605. Married (Joint): $0-$8,240 = 0; $8,240-$54,240 = 5.2% of excess over $8,240; over $54,240 = $2,392.00 + 5.58% of excess over $54,240. Period tables are the annual table divided by periods (weekly single: over $69 / $512; married: over $158 / $1,043). Result may be rounded to the nearest whole dollar. No K-4: withhold at Single rate with zero allowances.
income.deviations: Allowance values are tiered (first one or two allowances $9,160, others $2,320) depending on the Single/Joint allowance rate, so a single deductionPerAllowance cannot reproduce the official method. Brackets and standard deduction fit the generic model; the official per-period tables use rounded thresholds (e.g. semimonthly married $343 instead of $343.33), so annualized results can differ by about one cent (KW-100 example: $41.44 official vs $41.43 annualized).

sui.agency: Kansas Department of Labor (KDOL)
sui.notes: HB 2570 (2024): from 2026 the wage base is indexed to 25% of the statewide average annual wage (30% from 2028); 2026 = $15,100 (2025 was $14,000). New employers with less than 24 months of experience: 1.75%; new construction employers 5.55%. Rate schedule for 2026 per KDOL: HB 2570 Schedule C. Standard positive-balance rates run 0.0% (group 0) to 5.55% (group 27); negative groups 5.85% to 8.35%, then a solvency adjustment of -2.0% to +2.0% applies. The 2026 maximum rate is not filled in: confirm your rate with the Kansas Department of Labor (KDOL).

KS.deposit: Frequency by annual withholding: annual ($0-$200; due Jan 25), quarterly ($200.01-$1,200; due the 25th after each quarter), monthly ($1,200.01-$8,000; due the 15th of the next month), semi-monthly ($8,000.01-$100,000; 1st-15th due the 25th, 16th-end due the 10th of next month), quad-monthly ($100,000.01 and above; due within three banking days of the 7th, 15th, 21st and last day of the month). A KW-5 deposit report is required for every period even if zero.
KS.quarterlyReport: KW-5 Withholding Tax Deposit Report (per assigned frequency); KDOL K-CNS 100 Employer's Quarterly Wage Report and Unemployment Tax Return
KS.annualReconciliation: KW-3 Annual Withholding Tax Return (with W-2/1099 data), due January 31
KS.notes: KDOR Notice 25-06 (Oct 2025, implementing SB 269) concluded there is no rate reduction for tax year 2026, so the KW-100 (Rev. 10-24) tables remain in effect for 2026 and were also used for all of 2025. Supplemental: if supplemental wages are paid separately and federal withholding is a flat percentage, withhold Kansas at 5%; otherwise aggregate with regular wages. Confirm your unemployment rate and the quarterly unemployment report form (K-CNS 100) with the Kansas Department of Labor (KDOL).

KY.name: Kentucky

allowance.notes: Form K-4 has no allowances; it is used for exemption from withholding and additional withholding only.

income.formula: 2026 Kentucky Withholding Tax Formula (42A003(TCF)(10-2025)): annual wages = period wages x pay periods; Kentucky taxable wages = annual wages - $3,360 standard deduction; annual tax = taxable wages x 3.5%; withholding per period = annual tax / pay periods. Example: $3,270 monthly -> (39,240 - 3,360) x 3.5% / 12 = $104.65.
income.localTaxes: Local occupational license (payroll) taxes levied by many cities, counties and school districts (for example Louisville Metro, Lexington-Fayette); rates and rules vary by jurisdiction and are administered locally, not by the Department of Revenue. Not included here.

sui.agency: Kentucky Office of Unemployment Insurance (Education and Labor Cabinet)
sui.notes: Rate Schedule A in effect for 2026 (also 2020-2025): positive-reserve rates 0.30%-2.40%, negative-reserve rates 6.50%-9.00%. New employers at least 2.7% until 3 years of experience; new contract construction employers get the highest rate of the schedule in effect (9.00% under Schedule A). SCUF (Service Capacity Upgrade Fund) suspended for all of 2026; SB 129 reinstates SCUF for 2027 at 0.0115% (an allocation of the contribution, not an added cost). No surcharge while the trust fund is solvent. 2025 wage base was $11,700.

KY.deposit: Assigned by annual Kentucky withholding: annual (under $400/yr; Form K-3 due January 31), quarterly ($400-$1,999/yr; K-1 due last day of month after quarter), monthly ($2,000-$49,999/yr; K-1 due the 15th of next month), twice-monthly ($50,000 or more/yr; 1st-15th due the 25th, 16th-end due the 10th of next month). Employers accumulating $100,000 or more during any reporting period must remit within one banking day. Electronic filing and payment required.
KY.quarterlyReport: Form K-1, Employer's Return of Income Tax Withheld (per assigned frequency); OUI Form UI-3, Employer's Quarterly Unemployment Wage and Tax Report
KY.annualReconciliation: Form K-3, Employer's Return of Income Tax Withheld (Annual Reconciliation) for the last period of the year, plus W-2 data (Form K-5, 42A805, for employers issuing fewer than 26 statements), due January 31
KY.notes: 2025 values: flat 4.0%, standard deduction $3,270. Employees with more than one W-2 may need extra withholding of $117.60/yr because the standard deduction is claimed once. The 2026 employer instructions publish no supplemental rate, so SerieX adds supplemental wages to regular wages (bonuses are subject to withholding; many payroll programs use 3.5%: confirm with the Kentucky Department of Revenue before using a flat rate). No 2027 rate cut has been enacted yet (the HB 8 framework allows future 0.5-point cuts if budget triggers are met).

LA.name: Louisiana

code2_married_joint_qss_or_head_of_house.label: 2 - Married filing jointly, qualifying surviving spouse or head of household

allowance.notes: No dependents/allowances on the 2026 L-4. Block A code 0/1/2 selects the standard deduction. L-4 line 7 is a signed per-pay-period adjustment (increase or decrease of tax withheld; a decrease cannot take withholding below zero).

income.formula: R-1306 (1/26), effective on or after January 1, 2026, based on a 3.09% withholding rate: W = (S - (D / N)) x 0.0309, where S = wages per pay period, N = pay periods (daily 365, weekly 52, biweekly 26, semimonthly 24, monthly 12, annual 1), D = 0 (code 0 or no L-4), $12,875 (code 1: single or married filing separately), or $25,750 (code 2: married filing jointly, qualifying surviving spouse, head of household). Any negative variable is treated as zero. Then apply the L-4 line 7 adjustment. Employees with no L-4: no standard deduction.
income.deviations: Withholding rate 3.09% is higher than the 3.00% statutory individual rate (built-in cushion). Daily payroll uses 365 periods. L-4 line 7 allows a negative per-period adjustment.

sui.agency: Louisiana Workforce Commission (LWC)
sui.notes: 2026 wage base $7,000 (down from $7,700 in 2025). Total rates from the 2026 contribution rate table: positive reserve ratio 1.94% down to 0.09%; negative reserve ratio 2.20% up to 6.20% (each rate has a FUTA creditable factor; Incumbent Worker Training Program and Integrity social charges are included in the total rate but are not FUTA-creditable). New (ineligible) employers pay the average rate of their industrial classification until they complete the 24-month eligibility period, so there is no single new employer rate (generally at least 1% and at most 6.2%; confirm your rate with the Louisiana Workforce Commission).

LA.deposit: LDR assigns quarterly, monthly or semimonthly payment frequency; L-1 returns for quarterly and monthly payers are due the last day of the month following each quarter (e.g. Q1 2026 due April 30, 2026); semimonthly payers use the semimonthly L-1. Usual thresholds: semimonthly if average monthly withholding is $5,000 or more, monthly if $500 or more, otherwise quarterly; confirm your schedule with the Louisiana Department of Revenue (LDR). File and pay via LaTAP.
LA.quarterlyReport: Form L-1, Employer's Quarterly Return of Louisiana Withholding Tax; LWC Employer's Quarterly Report of Wages and Contributions (LWC-77)
LA.annualReconciliation: Form L-3, Employer's Annual Reconciliation (Transmittal of Withholding Tax Statements), with W-2s, due January 31
LA.notes: 2025 withholding (R-1306 1/25): same 3.09% formula with standard deductions $12,500 (code 1) and $25,000 (code 2). Act 11 of the 2024 Third Extraordinary Session set a flat 3% individual rate from 2025. LDR publishes no supplemental flat rate, so supplemental wages use the regular formula. New employers pay their industry average rate until they are eligible for their own rate, so no new employer rate is filled in: enter the rate the Louisiana Workforce Commission (LWC) assigned you in State settings. Confirm deposit thresholds and Form L-3 with LDR, and Form LWC-77 with the LWC. Daily payrolls are annualized with 365 days (Louisiana formula: daily payroll N = 365).

MA.name: Massachusetts

allowance.notes: Allowances = exemptions on Form M-4 (a claimed spouse counts as 4). Annual exemption factor: 0 exemptions = $0; 1 exemption = $4,400; more than 1 = $1,000 x number claimed + $3,400 (weekly: $85 for 1, else $19 x n + $66; biweekly $169 / $38n + $131; semimonthly $183 / $42n + $141; monthly $367 / $83n + $284; daily $12 / $3n + $9). A claimed spouse counts as 4 exemptions on Form M-4. Head of household: subtract $120/yr of tax (weekly $2.31, biweekly $4.62, semimonthly $5.00, monthly $10.00, daily $0.33). Blind employee and/or spouse: subtract $110/yr of tax each (weekly $2.12, biweekly $4.23, semimonthly $4.58, monthly $9.17, daily $0.30).

income.formula: Circular M (Rev. 12/25), percentage method for wages paid from January 1, 2026: 1) from period wages subtract amounts deducted for Social Security, Medicare, Massachusetts, U.S. or Railroad retirement systems, cumulative maximum $2,000 per year (stop once $2,000 reached); 2) subtract the exemption factor for the period; 3) annualize (52, 12, 24, 26 or 27); 4) annual tax = 5% of the result up to $1,107,750 plus 9% of the excess (4% surtax; 2026 threshold); 5) divide by periods; 6) subtract head-of-household tax value if applicable; 7) subtract blindness tax value per blind person. Do not withhold from employees claiming 1+ exemptions whose wages are below weekly $154, biweekly $308, semimonthly $333, monthly $667, daily $22, annual $8,000. Full-time students with annual income not over $8,000 and MSRRA-exempt employees (Form M-4-MS): no withholding. Supplemental wages paid separately: 5% (Circular M section G), or 9% on the part that pushes annualized regular + supplemental wages over $1,107,750.
income.deviations: Exemption value is $4,400 for the first exemption and $1,000 for each additional one (spouse = 4 exemptions); pre-tax deduction of FICA/Medicare/retirement contributions capped at $2,000 per year; fixed tax credits for head of household and blindness; $8,000 annual no-withholding threshold; 4% surtax bracket over $1,107,750.

sui.agency: Massachusetts Department of Unemployment Assistance (DUA)
sui.notes: 2026: new employers (registered less than 3 years) 2.42%; new construction-industry employers 6.08%; established employers: Schedule E, positive-reserve 0.94%-5.24%, negative-reserve 7.03%-14.37%. Experience-rated employers also pay the COVID-19 Recovery Assessment (varies by rate; combined UI + assessment 1.118%-17.086%); new employers paying new-employer rates are exempt from it. Deferral of up to 34% of Q1/Q2 contributions may be available. 2025 new employer rate was 2.13%.

programs.name: Paid Family and Medical Leave
programs.notes: 0.88% total for employers with 25+ covered individuals (employee up to 0.46%); fewer than 25: 0.46% employee only (set employer 0 in State settings).

programs.name: Employer Medical Assistance Contribution
programs.notes: Years 1-3 of UI liability exempt, year 4 0.12%, year 5 0.24%, year 6+ 0.34%; not owed with fewer than 6 employees in a quarter.

programs.name: Workforce Training Fund
programs.notes: Paid with quarterly UI contributions.

MA.deposit: Form M-941 frequency by expected annual withholding: annual if $100 or less (due January 31), quarterly if $101-$1,200 (due last day of month after quarter), monthly if $1,201-$25,000 (due the 15th of the next month, except March/June/September/December returns due the last day of the following month). Employers withholding more than $25,000 per year file and pay weekly (Form M-942; confirm with the Massachusetts Department of Revenue). All returns via MassTaxConnect.
MA.quarterlyReport: Form M-941 Employer's Return of Income Taxes Withheld (per frequency); DUA quarterly Employment and Wage Detail Report with UI/EMAC/WTF contributions (UI Online, due April 30 / July 31 / October 31 / January 31); PFML contribution return filed quarterly in MassTaxConnect
MA.annualReconciliation: Form M-3, Reconciliation of Massachusetts Income Taxes Withheld for Employers, with W-2 data, due January 31
MA.notes: 2025 surtax threshold was $1,083,150; the rest of Circular M is unchanged from 2025. The Workforce Training Fund rate is 0.056% of taxable wages (DUA Employer's Guide): confirm it on your DUA rate notice. COVID-19 Recovery Assessment (experience-rated employers only, rate from the DUA schedule) is not added by default; add it as a company rate when you owe it.

MD.name: Maryland

single.label: Single, married filing separately or dependent

joint.label: Married filing jointly, head of household or qualifying surviving spouse

allowance.notes: MW507 exemptions are $3,200 each per year (weekly $61.54, biweekly $123.08, semimonthly $133.33, monthly $266.67, daily $8.77). Employees expecting federal AGI over $100,000 ($150,000 joint) must use the MW507 worksheet to reduce exemptions.

income.formula: Comptroller 2026 Withholding Guide percentage method: 1) taxable = gross wages - standard deduction ($3,400/yr for every status; weekly $65.38, biweekly $130.76, semimonthly $141.66, monthly $283.33, daily $9.31) - (exemptions x $3,200/yr per-period equivalent); 2) apply the combined state+local percentage table for the employee's county of residence (state bracket rate + flat local rate). The state portion of the tables equals the brackets above (Maryland law tells the Comptroller to ignore state rates below 4.75% when building withholding schedules). Single = single, married filing separately, dependent; Joint = married filing jointly, head of household, qualifying surviving spouse. Do not withhold if annualized gross wages are under $5,000 (weekly $96, biweekly $192, semimonthly $208, monthly $417, daily $13.70). Local portion: Maryland residents - county rate (the guide provides tables for 2.25, 2.40, 2.65, 2.75, 2.85, 3.00, 3.05, 3.10, 3.20, 3.30%; use the table rate that equals or slightly exceeds the actual county rate); nonresidents working in Maryland (non-reciprocal states) - the special 2.25% nonresident rate (combined first bracket 7.00%); residents working in Delaware or another non-reciprocal state - special Delaware tables (credit for the other state's tax). No MW507 on file: highest local rate 3.30%. Lump-sum annual bonus: 6.50% state + the county's local rate.
income.deviations: State portion fits the generic model (standard deduction $3,400, $3,200 deduction per exemption, brackets above). The official method adds a county local tax (flat percentage of the same taxable income; graduated for Anne Arundel and Frederick) or the 2.25% special nonresident rate, has a $5,000 annual no-withholding threshold, and uses special tables for residents working in Delaware.
income.localTaxes: County/Baltimore City income tax withheld with state tax on the same taxable wages, by county of residence on MW507 (SerieX includes the 2026 county rates). Anne Arundel and Frederick have graduated local rates. Nonresidents: special nonresident rate 2.25% instead of a county rate.

sui.agency: Maryland Department of Labor, Division of Unemployment Insurance
sui.notes: Tax Table A (lowest) in effect for 2026 and 2025; contributory rates 0.30%-7.50%; standard rate 7.50% (failure to file). MD Labor states new employer rates may range from 1.0% to 2.6% depending on the table; for 2026 the new employer rate is 2.6%. Foreign (out-of-state headquartered) construction contractors pay the Maryland construction-industry average rate, not lower than the new employer rate.

MD.deposit: Accelerated: employers that withheld $15,000 or more in the preceding calendar year and have $700 or more accumulated must pay within three business days after the payroll (pay date); monthly: more than $700 withheld in any quarter; quarterly: less than $700 per quarter; annual: less than $250 per year (MW506 due January 31); seasonal by approval. Returns/payments via Maryland Tax Connect.
MD.quarterlyReport: Form MW506, Employer's Return of Income Tax Withheld (per assigned frequency); Employer's Quarterly Contribution and Employment Report filed in BEACON 2.0 (Division of Unemployment Insurance)
MD.annualReconciliation: Form MW508, Annual Employer Withholding Reconciliation Return, with W-2/1099 data, due January 31
MD.notes: 2025 values: withholding standard deduction $3,350; the new 6.25%/6.5% top brackets came from the 2025 legislative session. County rates are the 2026 rates from the Comptroller's Central Payroll Bureau memo (February 4, 2026). Confirm the quarterly unemployment report form (formerly DLLR/DUI 15) with the Maryland Department of Labor. Maryland withholding includes the county (local) income tax: enter the county rate in percent in the employee's County (local) tax rate field. SerieX uses the Comptroller table rate that equals or is slightly above it (nonresidents 2.25; blank = 3.30). Anne Arundel and Frederick have graduated local rates (use their top 3.20 table or enter a lower rate). FAMLI contributions start January 1, 2027 (none in 2026). Daily payrolls are annualized with 364 days (Maryland daily percentage tables use annual / 364).

ME.name: Maine

married_single.label: Married, but withholding at higher single rate

allowance.notes: Each W-4ME allowance subtracts $5,300 per year (2025: $5,150).

income.formula: MRS percentage method (Withholding Tables for Individual Income Tax 2026, REVISED August 2026): 1) annualize wages (52 weekly, 26 biweekly, 24 semimonthly, 12 monthly, 260 daily/misc); 2) allowances x $5,300; 3) standard deduction: single $12,850 if annualized wages <= $102,250, $0 if >= $177,250, otherwise $12,850 x ($177,250 - annual wages) / $75,000; married $28,550 if <= $204,550, $0 if >= $354,550, otherwise $28,550 x ($354,550 - annual wages) / $150,000 (round to 4 decimals); 4) annualized income = annual wages - step 2 - step 3; 5) tax: Single: under $27,400 = 5.80%; $27,400-$64,850 = $1,589 + 6.75% over $27,400; $64,850 and over = $4,117 + 7.15% over $64,850. Married: under $54,850 = 5.80%; $54,850-$129,750 = $3,181 + 6.75% over $54,850; $129,750 and over = $8,237 + 7.15% over $129,750; plus 2% surcharge on annualized income over $1,000,000 (single) / $1,500,000 (married); 6) divide by pay periods and ROUND TO THE NEAREST DOLLAR. 'Married, but withholding at higher single rate' and 'Single or Head of Household' use the single schedule. Invalid/missing W-4ME: single with zero allowances.
income.deviations: Standard deduction phases out linearly with annualized wages; 2% surcharge on very high annualized income; result rounded to whole dollars. The official schedule uses rounded base amounts ($1,589 and $4,117 single; $3,181 and $8,237 married), so a pure marginal computation can differ by less than $1 per year before rounding (MRS example 2: official $1,667/yr vs $1,666.83 marginal; both give $32/week). Otherwise generic.

sui.agency: Maine Department of Labor, Bureau of Unemployment Compensation
sui.notes: All rates are COMBINED rates = UI rate + Competitive Skills Scholarship Fund (CSSF) 0.14% + Unemployment Program Administrative Fund (UPAF) 0.17%. 2026 new employer rate 2.23% UI + 0.14% CSSF + 0.17% UPAF = 2.54%. Experience categories range from 0.31% (category 01: 0.00% UI) to 6.60% (category 20: 6.29% UI). Schedule A (lowest schedule) applies for 2026. Do not add CSSF/UPAF again.

programs.name: Paid Family and Medical Leave
programs.notes: Employers with 15+ covered employees remit 1.0% (up to half from employees); fewer than 15: 0.5% that may be all employee-paid (set employer 0 in State settings).

ME.deposit: Semiweekly (federal-style: wages paid Wed-Fri due the following Wednesday; Sat-Tue due the following Friday) if total withholding during the lookback period July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025 was $18,000 or more; all other employers pay on or before the quarterly return due date. Electronic payment required if combined annual Maine tax liability is $10,000 or more. Quarterly returns must be filed electronically.
ME.quarterlyReport: Form 941ME, Employer's Return of Maine Income Tax Withheld (quarterly, due last day of month after the quarter) and Form ME UC-1, Unemployment Contributions Report (quarterly); PFML wages/contributions reported quarterly in the Maine PFML portal
ME.annualReconciliation: No separate annual reconciliation return; withholding is reconciled on each quarterly 941ME and W-2/1099 data must be filed electronically by January 31
ME.notes: MID-YEAR CHANGE: MRS revised the 2026 withholding methods on August 13, 2026 (L.D. 2212), retroactive to January 1, 2026, and asked employers to implement them as soon as possible. The earlier version (Revised December 2025) used withholding standard deductions of $12,450 single / $27,750 married with the same phase-out ranges and brackets and no surcharge. Supplemental wages paid separately may be withheld at a flat 5%; backup withholding 5%. The Maine UI wage base is $12,000 (Maine Department of Labor). SerieX uses the August 13, 2026 revision for all 2026 paychecks. UI rates are combined rates (CSSF and UPAF included).

MI.name: Michigan

allowance.notes: MI-W4 personal and dependency exemptions are $5,900 each per year in 2026 ($5,800 in 2025). Employees may not claim more exemptions than on their MI-1040; special exemptions (e.g. disability) are part of the count.

income.formula: Form 446 (2026 Michigan Income Tax Withholding Guide): withholding = (wages for the period - (exemptions x $5,900 / pay periods)) x 4.25%, not below zero, plus any additional amount. Bonuses and other payments made separately from regular payroll: multiply the payment by 4.25% with no adjustment for exemptions.
income.localTaxes: 24 Michigan cities levy a city income tax under the Uniform City Income Tax Ordinance, withheld by employers separately from state tax (e.g. Detroit 2.4% resident / 1.2% nonresident; Grand Rapids 1.5% / 0.75%). City rates and forms are administered by each city (Detroit by the Michigan Treasury). Not included here; confirm city rates with each city.

sui.agency: Michigan Unemployment Insurance Agency (UIA)
sui.notes: Taxable wage base $9,000 for qualified employers (all reports filed and no balance of $25 or more owed as of the February cutoff; Feb 13, 2026); delinquent employers are taxed on $9,500. New employers 2.7% for the first two years of liability (year 3: 1/3 CBC + 1.8%; year 4: 2/3 CBC + 1.0%); new construction employers pay the average construction contractor rate, 5.0% for 2026. Experienced employer range 0.06%-12.2% for 2026 (0.06%-10.3% in 2025). Confirm your rate with the Michigan Unemployment Insurance Agency (UIA).

MI.deposit: Treasury assigns a filing frequency (monthly or quarterly, accelerated EFT for large filers) for the combined Sales, Use and Withholding (SUW) return; returns/payments due the 20th of the month after the period. Confirm your assigned filing frequency with the Michigan Department of Treasury.
MI.quarterlyReport: Form 5080, Sales, Use and Withholding Taxes Monthly/Quarterly Return (per assigned frequency, via Michigan Treasury Online); UIA Form 1028, Employer's Quarterly Wage/Tax Report (MiWAM)
MI.annualReconciliation: Form 5081, Sales, Use and Withholding Taxes Annual Return (due February 28); W-2/1099 income record forms due to Treasury by January 31 (electronic if 10 or more)
MI.notes: Income tax withholding: 4.25%, with $5,900 per exemption per year (Michigan Department of Treasury). Confirm your unemployment rate (new construction employers 5.0%; range 0.06%-12.2%) and Form 1028 with the Michigan Unemployment Insurance Agency (UIA), deposit due dates and Forms 5080 / 5081 with the Michigan Department of Treasury, and city tax rates with each city.

MN.name: Minnesota

single.label: Single; married but withhold at higher single rate

allowance.notes: Each Form W-4MN allowance subtracts $5,300 per year (2025: $5,200). Employees without a W-4MN (federal W-4 no longer provides allowances): single with zero allowances.

income.formula: 2026 Minnesota Withholding Computer Formula: 1) period wages; 2) annualize (daily 360, weekly 52, biweekly 26, semimonthly 24, monthly 12, annual 1); 3) allowances x $5,300; 4) step 2 - step 3 (if zero or less, no tax); 5) Single: over $4,700 to $38,010: 5.35% of excess over $4,700; $38,010-$114,130: $1,782.09 + 6.80% over $38,010; $114,130-$207,850: $6,958.25 + 7.85% over $114,130; over $207,850: $14,315.27 + 9.85% over $207,850. Married: over $14,700 to $63,400: 5.35% over $14,700; $63,400-$208,180: $2,605.45 + 6.80% over $63,400; $208,180-$352,630: $12,450.49 + 7.85% over $208,180; over $352,630: $23,789.82 + 9.85% over $352,630; 6) divide by the periods used in step 2 (may round to the nearest dollar). Supplemental payments made separately: flat 6.25%.
income.deviations: Fits the generic model (the 0% first bracket replaces a standard deduction: single $4,700, married $14,700). Daily payroll uses 360 periods. 'Married but withhold at higher Single rate' uses the single table.

sui.agency: Minnesota Department of Employment and Economic Development (DEED), Unemployment Insurance Minnesota
sui.notes: UI tax rate = experience rate (or new employer rate) + base tax rate 0.40% (2026). New employer rates are assigned by industry (2026: most non-construction industries 1.00%; e.g. mining 4.06%, admin & support 2.04%; construction 1.98%-8.90% by NAICS). The new employer rate shown (1.40%) is the typical 1.00% plus the 0.40% base rate. Experience rates 0.00%-8.90% (+0.40% base => 0.40%-9.30%). An Additional Assessment of 14.00% of the UI tax before assessments applies for 2026; no Special (federal loan interest) Assessment. Total UI tax due is truncated to whole dollars. 2025: wage base $43,000, base rate 0.40%.

programs.name: Minnesota Paid Leave
programs.notes: 0.88% total; employer pays at least 50%. Small employers: 0.66% total (employer at least 0.22%) - set in State settings.

programs.name: Workforce Enhancement Fee
programs.notes: 0.10% of UI taxable wages (not owed by reimbursing employers).

programs.name: UI Additional Assessment
programs.notes: 14% of the UI tax before assessments: SerieX uses 14% of your company UI rate (0.196% at the default 1.40%).

MN.agencyUnemployment: Minnesota Department of Employment and Economic Development
