MN.deposit: Follows the federal schedule when more than $1,500 of Minnesota tax was withheld in the previous quarter: semiweekly (Wed/Fri) if the IRS requires semiweekly, monthly (by the 15th) if the IRS requires monthly. If $1,500 or less was withheld in the previous quarter, the whole quarter may be deposited with the quarterly due date (April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31). Annual filers ($500 or less in the prior year) pay by January 31 but must deposit whenever accumulated tax exceeds $500. Electronic payment required in many cases.
MN.quarterlyReport: Minnesota withholding tax quarterly return (e-Services); Unemployment Insurance Minnesota Quarterly UI Wage Detail Report (also used for Paid Leave premiums)
MN.annualReconciliation: No separate reconciliation form: W-2 information must be submitted to the Department of Revenue by January 31 (annual filers file their annual return by January 31)
MN.notes: Minnesota Paid Leave is new for 2026. Minnesota has not adopted the 2025 federal tax law changes for withholding purposes (W-4MN required). Daily payrolls are annualized with 360 days (Minnesota computer formula: 360 if paid by the day).

MO.name: Missouri

allowance.notes: MO W-4 has no allowances (filing status, 'spouse does not work' check box on line 1, additional withholding on line 2, exemption).

income.formula: 2026 Missouri Withholding Tax Formula: 1) annual wage = period wages x periods (daily 260, weekly 52, biweekly 26, semimonthly 24, monthly 12); 2) subtract standard deduction: single / married spouse works / married filing separate $16,100; married spouse does not work (MO W-4 line 1 box) $32,200; head of household $24,150; 3) apply annual rates cumulatively: 0% on $0-$1,348; 2.0% on $1,348-$2,696; 2.5% to $4,044; 3.0% to $5,392; 3.5% to $6,740; 4.0% to $8,088; 4.5% to $9,436; 4.7% over $9,436; 4) divide by periods; withholding MUST be rounded to the nearest whole dollar. DOR example: married (spouse works) $35,000/yr -> taxable $18,900 -> $263 (sum of rounded bracket amounts) + 4.7% x $9,464 = $707.81/yr -> $59/month. Supplemental wages paid separately: flat 4.7% or the aggregate method.
income.deviations: Withholding rounded to whole dollars; the DOR worked example rounds each bracket's tax to whole dollars before summing (fixed amounts: $27, $34, $40, $47, $54, $61; total $263 through $9,436), which can differ by cents from exact computation.
income.localTaxes: Kansas City and City of St. Louis earnings taxes (1% each on residents and on nonresidents working in the city; administered by the cities, not the DOR); confirm current rates with each city.

sui.agency: Missouri Department of Labor and Industrial Relations, Division of Employment Security (DES)
sui.notes: 2026 new employer rates (include contribution rate adjustment): 2.376% for all industries including mining and construction; nonprofit 501(c)(3) 1.00%. Experienced rates 0%-6% before the maximum-rate surcharge (employers at the maximum for consecutive years) and contribution rate adjustments. Wage base by year: 2026 $9,000, 2025 $9,500, 2024 $10,000 (statutory range $7,000-$13,000 depending on trust fund). No federal interest assessment expected for 2026.

MO.deposit: Quarter-monthly payments (90% of tax for each quarter-monthly period within 3 banking days after the period ends: 1st-7th, 8th-15th, 16th-22nd, 23rd-end) if $9,000 or more was withheld in each of at least two months of the prior 12 months; monthly if $500 or more per month; quarterly if at least $100 per quarter; annual if less than $100 per quarter. Form MO-941 filed per period (even with no withholding).
MO.quarterlyReport: Form MO-941, Employer's Return of Income Taxes Withheld (monthly/quarterly/annual); DES Form MODES-4-7, Quarterly Contribution and Wage Report
MO.annualReconciliation: Form MO W-3, Transmittal of Tax Statements, with W-2s, due January 31
MO.notes: 2026 standard deductions follow the federal amounts as changed by the 2025 federal law (OBBBA). Top rate unchanged at 4.7% for 2026; brackets were inflation-adjusted. Confirm the quarterly unemployment report form (MODES-4-7) with the Missouri Division of Employment Security.

MS.name: Mississippi

allowance.notes: Allowances = the TOTAL DOLLAR exemption amount from Form 89-350 line 6 (e.g. 12000). Form 89-350 line 6 gives a TOTAL DOLLAR exemption amount (EX) that is subtracted from annualized wages: single $6,000; married $12,000 (when both spouses work they split it); head of family $9,500; plus $1,500 for each dependent and for age 65+/blind boxes. Use the dollar amount directly.

income.formula: DOR Computer Payroll Accounting flowchart for periods in 2026 (revised 8/13/25): STDED = $2,300 single (S), $4,600 married one spouse employed (M), $2,300 married both spouses employed (B), $3,400 head of family (H); AGP = period pay x periods (annual 1, monthly 12, semimonthly 24, biweekly 26, weekly 52, daily/misc 260); TI = AGP - (EX + STDED); if TI <= $10,000 tax = 0, else TAX = (TI - 10,000) x 4.0%; PWT = TAX / periods, rounded to whole dollars; add any agreed additional amount. Miscellaneous (daily) payrolls: multiply the daily result by the number of days worked.
income.deviations: Fits the generic model with a 0% bracket for the first $10,000 of taxable income and the exemption entered as a dollar amount. Withholding is rounded to whole dollars.

sui.agency: Mississippi Department of Employment Security (MDES)
sui.notes: New employers: 1.00% first year of liability, 1.10% second year, 1.20% third and later years until eligible for a modified (experience) rate. Modified rates 0.0%-5.4% (never below the general experience ratio). These rates EXCLUDE the Workforce Investment and Training contribution (listed under other state taxes). Wage base $14,000 (unchanged from 2025); confirm it with the Mississippi Department of Employment Security (MDES).

programs.name: Workforce Investment and Training
programs.notes: 0.20% in addition to the UI rate (0.16% when the 0.04% Mississippi Works part does not apply).

MS.deposit: Monthly Form 89-105 returns/payments (due the 15th of the following month) for employers with average liability of $300 or more per month; smaller employers may file quarterly; returns via Taxpayer Access Point (TAP). Confirm your thresholds and due dates with the Mississippi Department of Revenue.
MS.quarterlyReport: Form 89-105, Employer's Withholding Tax Return (monthly or quarterly via TAP); MDES UI-2 Quarterly Contribution (Tax) Report with UI-3 Wage List
MS.annualReconciliation: Form 89-140, Annual Information Return (W-2/1099 reconciliation), due January 31
MS.notes: Rate history: 4.4% for 2025, 4.0% for 2026; scheduled 3.75% for 2027 and further 0.25-point cuts to 3.0% by 2030. Mississippi publishes no supplemental flat rate, so supplemental wages are added to regular wages. Confirm the UI-2 / UI-3 unemployment forms with the Mississippi Department of Employment Security (MDES).

MT.name: Montana

married.label: Married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse

married_both_working.label: Married filing jointly, both spouses work (line 2 box)

allowance.notes: Montana dropped withholding allowances/exemptions (2024 redesign). The 2026 Form MW-4 captures only filing status (line 1a single or married filing separately, 1b married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse, 1c head of household), a line-2 box for married couples where both spouses work (withhold on the single table), additional withholding, and exemption claims (exemptions must be renewed every year).

income.formula: Official per-period formula W = A + B x (G - C) from the Employer and Information Agent Guide tables. Annual equivalent: (1) annualize gross taxable wages; (2) subtract the 2026 federal standard deduction for the MW-4 status: $16,100 single / married filing separately / married filing jointly with both spouses working (line 2), $32,200 married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse (line 1b), $24,150 head of household (line 1c); (3) tax 4.7% on taxable wages up to $47,500 (single), $95,000 (married), $71,250 (head of household) and 5.65% on the excess; (4) divide by pay periods; (5) round to a whole dollar; (6) add MW-4 extra withholding. Published annual table: single 0% to $16,100, 4.7% $16,100-$63,600, $2,233 + 5.65% over $63,600; married 0% to $32,200, 4.7% to $127,200, $4,465 + 5.65% over $127,200; head of household 0% to $24,150, 4.7% to $95,400, $3,349 + 5.65% over $95,400. Published period thresholds (single): monthly $1,342 / $5,300 (base $187), semimonthly $671 / $2,650 ($94), biweekly $619 / $2,446 ($86), weekly $310 / $1,223 ($43), daily $62 / $245 ($9).
income.deviations: Results are rounded to whole dollars (guide text says 'rounded up' but its worked examples round to the nearest dollar). Married employees whose spouse also works use the single table. The guide's annual wage-bracket table does not exactly match the formula at low wages; the guide states the formula reproduces the tables with insignificant rounding variances, so use the formula.

sui.agency: Montana Department of Labor & Industry, Unemployment Insurance Division (Contributions Bureau)
sui.notes: 2026 uses rate Schedule 1 (rates 0.00%-6.12%, average 0.95%). New employers get their industry rate: Agriculture/Forestry/Fishing 1.30%, Mining 1.30%, Construction 2.00%, Manufacturing 1.00%, Utilities/Transportation/Warehousing 1.00%, Wholesale 1.00%, Retail 1.00%, Finance/Insurance/Real Estate 1.00%, Services 1.10%, Unclassified 2.00% (1.00% is the default shown). Wage base = 80% of the 2024 average annual wage. The Administrative Fund Tax is charged on top (listed under other state taxes). Employers delinquent at rate calculation get a penalty rate 50% higher. 2025 wage base was $45,100.

programs.name: Administrative Fund Tax
programs.notes: 0.18% for new employers, classes 03-10 and deficit employers; 0.13% for classes 01-02.

MT.deposit: Schedule set by total withheld in the July 1-June 30 lookback period: $12,000 or more = accelerated (same dates as the federal deposit schedule); $1,200-$11,999 = monthly, due the 15th of the following month; $1,199 or less = annual, due January 31. New businesses pay monthly until a lookback period exists. Pay through the TransAction Portal (TAP), ACH credit, or check with voucher MW-1.
MT.quarterlyReport: No quarterly withholding return (payments only on the assigned schedule). UI: Unemployment Insurance Quarterly Wage Report (UI-5) to the Department of Labor & Industry.

MT.notes: HB 337 (2025) cut the top rate to 5.65% for 2026 (5.9% in 2025). Already-enacted 2027 rates (Publication 1, 2026): 4.7% on taxable income up to $65,000 single / $130,000 married filing jointly / $97,500 head of household, 5.4% above; 2027 withholding tables are not published yet. The Department recommends a new MW-4 every year.

married.label: Married filing jointly or surviving spouse

sui.notes: Experience rate = 1.9% base rate minus the employer reserve ratio percentage (reserve ratio x 0.68), bounded 0.06%-5.76%. Rate notices sent November 17, 2025; voluntary contributions were due December 17, 2025. 2025 wage base $32,600.

NC.agencyUnemployment: North Carolina Division of Employment Security
NC.deposit: Average monthly withholding under $250: quarterly Form NC-5 (due last day of month after quarter, January 31 for Q4). $250 to under $2,000: monthly NC-5 due the 15th of the following month (December due January 31). $2,000 or more: semiweekly, paid on the federal semiweekly dates (Form NC-5P / EFT) with quarterly NC-5Q. NC.notes: Already enacted: S.L. 2026-41 (signed July 7, 2026) sets the individual rate at 3.49% for 2027-2029, 3.24% for 2030-2032 and 2.99% from 2033 (replacing revenue triggers). NCDOR has not published 2027 withholding tables yet (the withholding rate is normally the statutory rate plus 0.1%, which would be 3.59%: confirm with NCDOR). 2025 statutory rate was 4.25%.

ND.name: North Dakota

allowance.notes: Only for employees still on a pre-2020 federal Form W-4: subtract $5,050 per allowance per year (weekly $97, biweekly $194, semimonthly $210, monthly $420, quarterly $1,268, semiannual $2,525, daily $19), then use the single table (single includes head of household) or married table. For 2020-or-later Forms W-4 there are no allowances (count = 0) and the table for the Step 1(c) filing status is used; a new hire with no W-4 is treated as single.

income.formula: 2026 Withholding Rates & Instructions, percentage method for 2020+ Forms W-4: (1) taxable wages for the period x number of pay periods = annual wage; (2) annual withholding from the table for the W-4 Step 1(c) status - married filing jointly: 0 to $57,500, 1.95% of excess over $57,500, $2,164.99 + 2.50% over $168,525; head of household: 0 to $78,475, 1.95% over $78,475, $4,118.40 + 2.50% over $289,675; single (or married filing separately): 0 to $57,625, 1.95% over $57,625, $3,916.09 + 2.50% over $258,450; (3) divide by pay periods and round to the nearest dollar. Pre-2020 W-4: subtract allowances first, then single table (0 to $57,625; 1.95%; $3,916.09 + 2.50% over $258,450) or married table (0 to $57,500; 1.95%; $2,164.99 + 2.50% over $168,525).
income.deviations: Two methods depending on the W-4 version (pre-2020 with allowances vs 2020+ without). Withholding under $1.00 need not be withheld. Wages of Minnesota and Montana residents for work in North Dakota are exempt under reciprocity.

sui.agency: Job Service North Dakota
sui.notes: New employer rates: non-construction 1.00% (positive balance) or 6.07% (negative balance); construction 9.67%. Positive-balance experienced employers 0.07%-1.10%; negative-balance 6.07%-9.67%. Wage base = 70% of the statewide average wage. 2025: base $45,100, new rates 1.03% / 6.09% / 9.69%.

ND.deposit: Form 306 filed and paid electronically each quarter (required when prior-year withholding was $1,000 or more, or when a third-party payroll provider files federal returns); a return is required even for quarters with no wages. Due by the last day of the month after the quarter; confirm the due date with the North Dakota Office of State Tax Commissioner.

ND.notes: Supplemental option 1 is a flat 1.50%; option 2 is the aggregate method. 2027 withholding tables and wage base are not published yet.

NE.name: Nebraska

allowance.notes: Value of one allowance for 2026: daily $9.38, weekly $46.92, biweekly $93.85, semimonthly $101.67, monthly $203.33, quarterly $610.00, semiannual $1,220.00, annual $2,440.00. 'Single' includes head of household; 'married' includes surviving spouse. Allowances come from Form W-4N; employees whose federal W-4 predates 2020 and who never filed a W-4N keep using federal status/allowances; employees with a 2020+ federal W-4 but no W-4N are withheld as single with 0 allowances.

income.formula: Circular EN 2026 percentage method: (1) taxable wages for the period (same as federal taxable wages); (2) subtract allowances x the period allowance value; (3) apply the period percentage table for single or married. Annual table (Table 7): single - not over $3,430 = 0; $3,430-$6,710 2.26%; $6,710-$21,810 $74.13 + 3.22%; $21,810-$31,610 $560.35 + 4.21%; $31,610-$40,130 $972.93 + 4.35%; $40,130-$75,370 $1,343.55 + 4.48%; over $75,370 $2,922.30 + 4.60%. Married - not over $8,190 = 0; $8,190-$13,010 2.26%; $13,010-$32,400 $108.93 + 3.22%; $32,400-$50,400 $733.29 + 4.21%; $50,400-$62,530 $1,491.09 + 4.35%; $62,530-$82,920 $2,018.75 + 4.48%; over $82,920 $2,932.22 + 4.60%. Example weekly single thresholds: $66 / $129 / $419 / $608 / $772 / $1,449. Employers may also use annualized, average-estimated, cumulative or part-year methods if used federally.
income.deviations: Special minimum withholding rule: employers with more than 24 employees must withhold at least 1.5% of each employee's taxable wages unless the employee documents a lower liability; when the computed amount is under 1.5% of wages, withholding must be at least 50% of the amount for a single employee with 1 allowance or a married employee with 2 allowances (wage-bracket tables shade the amounts that fail this test).

sui.agency: Nebraska Department of Labor, Office of Unemployment Insurance
sui.notes: New employer rate 1.25% non-construction, 5.40% construction. Rates are 'combined' rates (UI contribution plus State Unemployment Insurance Tax, SUIT; 20% of the combined rate is allocated to SUIT for 2026) - do not add SUIT separately. 20 rate categories from 0.00% (category 1) to 5.40% (category 20); category 12 average is 0.55%. Category 20 employers (including employers missing quarterly reports at rate calculation) pay on the first $24,000 of wages instead of $9,000. 2025 wage base was also $9,000/$24,000.

NE.deposit: Monthly deposit (Form 501N or EFT) due the 15th of the following month for the first and second months of a quarter when more than $500 was withheld in that month (or in the first month for the second-month test); the third month is paid with the quarterly Form 941N. Employers licensed as annual filers file one 941N by January 31. EFT is mandatory once total payments in a prior year exceeded $5,000.
NE.quarterlyReport: Form 941N Nebraska Income Tax Withholding Return (due April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31). UI: Combined Tax Report UI-11T with Wage Report UI-11W.
NE.annualReconciliation: Form W-3N Nebraska Reconciliation of Income Tax Withheld with state copies of W-2/1099, due January 31 (e-file required with more than 50 forms).
NE.notes: 2027 Circular EN already published (wages paid on/after January 1, 2027): allowance $2,510/year (weekly $48.27, biweekly $96.54, semimonthly $104.58, monthly $209.17, daily $9.65); rates 2.26%, 3.22%, 3.69%, 3.81%, 3.93%, 4.03%; annual single thresholds $3,530 / $6,910 / $22,450 / $32,540 / $41,310 / $77,590 (bases $0, $76.39, $576.78, $949.10, $1,283.24, $2,709.04); annual married thresholds $8,430 / $13,390 / $33,360 / $51,890 / $64,370 / $85,370 (bases $0, $112.10, $755.13, $1,438.89, $1,914.38, $2,739.68). The 2027 supplemental flat rate remains 3.5%. Nebraska gambling winnings withholding is also 3.5%. SerieX does not apply the minimum withholding rule for employers with more than 24 employees (at least 1.5% of wages): check it yourself if it applies to your company.

NH.name: New Hampshire

income.formula: No tax on wages; the Interest and Dividends Tax was repealed for periods after 2024. No state withholding.

sui.agency: New Hampshire Employment Security (NHES)
sui.notes: New employer base rate is 2.7% minus the Fund Balance (Trust Fund) Reduction for the quarter; the reduction was 1.0% for Q1 and Q2 2026 (net 1.7%) and only applies to accounts in compliance. Confirm the Q3-Q4 2026 reduction with New Hampshire Employment Security (NHES). Rates include the Administrative Contribution (AC) portion (minimum 0.1%, maximum 0.4%; e.g. net 1.7% = 0.4% AC + 1.3% UI) - do not add AC on top. Negative-rated employers also pay a 0.5% Inverse Minimum Rate surcharge (Q2 2026), giving the 7.5% maximum. Experience rates are assigned on a July-June fiscal year (2026-27 notices mailed August 27, 2026). The 2026 wage base is $14,000.

NH.deposit: No income tax withholding. UI tax is paid quarterly with the quarterly tax and wage report (due the last day of the month after the quarter).
NH.quarterlyReport: Employer Quarterly Tax and Wage Report filed through NHES WebTax.
NH.notes: Granite State Paid Family Leave is a voluntary insurance plan, not a payroll tax. Confirm your unemployment rate with New Hampshire Employment Security (NHES).

NJ.name: New Jersey

rate_A.label: Rate A (single, or married/civil union partner filing separately)

rate_B.label: Rate B (married filing jointly, head of household, qualifying widow(er))

allowance.notes: Value of one allowance per period: weekly $19.20, biweekly $38.40, semimonthly $41.60, monthly $83.30, quarterly $250, semiannual $500, annual $1,000, daily/miscellaneous $2.70. Allowances come from NJ-W4 line 4.

income.formula: NJ-WT percentage method: (1) multiply the period allowance value (weekly $19.20, biweekly $38.40, semimonthly $41.60, monthly $83.30, quarterly $250, semiannual $500, annual $1,000, daily/miscellaneous $2.70) by the allowances on NJ-W4; (2) subtract from period wages; (3) apply the New Jersey withholding rate table of that payroll period ("Tables for Percentage Method of Withholding", wages paid on and after October 1, 2020) selected by NJ-W4: status box 1 (single) or 3 (married/civil union partner separate) = Rate A; box 2 (married joint), 4 (head of household) or 5 (qualifying widow(er)) = Rate B unless the employee wrote a letter A-E on line 3 from the NJ-W4 wage chart; (4) add NJ-W4 line 5 extra withholding. The period tables round their thresholds to dollars and most bases to whole dollars, so they differ from the annual table divided by the periods; the daily table uses 365 days. The annual statuses above are the annual payroll period table.
income.deviations: Statuses are the five state rate tables (A-E) rather than filing statuses; the table is chosen from NJ-W4 as described. No flat supplemental rate: supplemental wages paid with regular wages are combined; supplemental wages paid separately are withheld at the table rate without allowances. Employees writing EXEMPT on NJ-W4 line 6 (annual, income $10,000 or less single/separate, $20,000 or less other statuses) are not withheld.

sui.agency: New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development, Division of Employer Accounts
sui.notes: Employer rates run on a July-June fiscal year. FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-27 (from July 1, 2026) both use Table C; NJDOL reported rates unchanged July 1, 2026. Commonly quoted totals (new employer 2.8%, experienced 0.5%-5.8%) include the 0.1175% employer Workforce Development/Supplemental Workforce Fund (WF/SWF) share, listed separately under other state taxes; the minimum and maximum shown are those totals minus 0.1175%. New employers keep the new rate for 3 calendar years. Employee UI 0.3825% (governmental reimbursable employers: 0.0825%). Maximum 2026 employee UI + WF/SWF deduction $190.40. 2025 wage bases: $43,300 (UI) and $165,400 (TDI/FLI employee).

programs.notes: Employee 0.0425% on the UI wage base; employer 0.1175% (part of the commonly quoted 2.8% new employer total).

programs.notes: Employee 0.19% up to $171,100.

programs.name: Temporary Disability Insurance Company

programs.name: Family Leave Insurance
programs.notes: Employee-only 0.23% up to $171,100.

NJ.agencyUnemployment: New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development
NJ.deposit: Monthly payment (Form NJ-500, electronic) by the 15th of the following month when more than $500 was withheld in the first and/or second month of the quarter; the third month is paid with the quarterly return. 'Weekly' payers (prior-year withholding of $10,000 or more) pay according to their pay frequency and file NJ-927-W. Electronic filing and payment required.
NJ.quarterlyReport: NJ-927 (or NJ-927-W) Employer's Quarterly Report covering income tax and UI/WF/SWF/DI/FLI contributions, plus WR-30 Employer Report of Wages Paid; due the 30th day of the month after the quarter (no weekend/holiday extension for NJDOL).

Already-announced 2027 values: UI/WF/SWF and employer TDI wage base $46,400; employee TDI/FLI wage base $177,100; FY 2026-27 new employer rates UI 2.6825%, DI 0.50%, WF/SWF 0.1175%, FLI 0. 2027 employee rates were not yet published ('available later this year'). No supplemental flat rate: supplemental wages are added to regular wages. SerieX uses the published per-period tables and allowance values; a pay period without a published table uses the annual table.

NM.name: New Mexico

allowance.notes: New Mexico uses the federal Form W-4; the 2026 tables no longer subtract allowance amounts. Employees may request extra withholding on a copy of the federal W-4 marked 'For New Mexico State Withholding Only'.

income.formula: FYI-104 (effective January 1, 2026) percentage method: pick the payroll-period table and the federal W-4 filing status (single, married, head of household) and apply 'base + rate x excess over threshold' to taxable wages for the period; add requested extra withholding. Annual table: single 0 to $8,050; 1.5% over $8,050; $82.50 + 3.2% over $13,550 (also $306.50 + 3.2% over $20,550, same rate); $434.50 + 4.3% over $24,550; $1,165.50 + 4.7% over $41,550; $2,716.50 + 4.9% over $74,550; $9,748.00 + 5.9% over $218,050. Married: 0 to $16,100; 1.5% over $16,100; $120 + 3.2% over $24,100; $664 + 4.3% over $41,100; $1,739 + 4.7% over $66,100; $4,089 + 4.9% over $116,100; $14,624 + 5.9% over $331,100. Head of household: 0 to $12,075; 1.5%; $120 + 3.2% over $20,075; $664 + 4.3% over $37,075; $1,739 + 4.7% over $62,075; $4,089 + 4.9% over $112,075; $14,624 + 5.9% over $327,075. Weekly single: 0 to $155, then 1.5% / 3.2% over $261 / 4.3% over $472 / 4.7% over $799 / 4.9% over $1,434 / 5.9% over $4,193. The tables embed a zero-rate amount (half the 2026 federal standard deduction) and the statutory 2025+ brackets (single 1.5% to $5,500, 3.2% to $16,500, 4.3% to $33,500, 4.7% to $66,500, 4.9% to $210,000, 5.9% above; married/HOH 1.5% to $8,000, 3.2% to $25,000, 4.3% to $50,000, 4.7% to $100,000, 4.9% to $315,000, 5.9% above).
income.deviations: Tables show some brackets split with the same rate (e.g. 3.2% band split at $20,550 single) - harmless. If federal withholding on supplemental wages uses the flat percentage, use a flat 5.9% for New Mexico; otherwise use the same method as federal. A married employee withheld at the single rate federally must also use the single table. No withholding required when the month's total for an employee is under $1. Nonresidents working 15 or fewer days in NM per year are not subject to withholding. The FYI-104 semimonthly table has an inconsistent first line ("not over $304" vs first bracket starting at $335) - use annualization.

sui.agency: New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions (DWS)
sui.notes: New contributing employers pay the greater of their industry's average rate or 1.0% until 2 years of experience. 2026 new employer industry rates: Agriculture 1.19, Construction 1.21, Transportation/Warehousing 1.15, Information 1.08, Administrative/Support/Waste 1.19, Public Administration 1.28, all other sectors 1.00. Experienced rates 0.33%-5.40% (reserve factor 3.6361 for 2026); employers whose computed rate exceeds 5.4% also pay an excess claims premium of up to 1% of taxable payroll (effective maximum 6.4%). 2025 wage base $33,200.

NM.agencyWithholding: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department
NM.agencyUnemployment: New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions
NM.deposit: TRD-41414 Wage Withholding Tax Return and payment due the 25th of the month after the reporting period; the period is monthly, quarterly or semiannual as assigned by TRD at registration. From 2026 all withholding returns, payments and reports must be filed electronically (TAP).
NM.quarterlyReport: TRD-41431 Workers' Compensation Fee Return and Employees Quarterly Wage and Withholding Report (new from Q1 2026, replaces WC-1 and TRD-31109; due the 25th after the quarter). NM.notes: Withholding gambling winnings: 6%. The FYI-104 does not address federal W-4 Step 3/4 entries for state purposes beyond allowing Step 4(c) extra withholding. Workers' compensation fee ($2.00 employee / $2.30 employer per employee per quarter) is a flat quarterly amount, not calculated per paycheck.

NV.name: Nevada

income.formula: No state income tax on wages; no state withholding.

sui.agency: Nevada Department of Employment, Training and Rehabilitation (DETR), Employment Security Division
sui.notes: New employers keep 2.95% for 14-17 calendar quarters, then get one of 18 experience rates from 0.25% to 5.40%. The 0.05% Career Enhancement Program (CEP) charge is separate (new employers pay 3.00% in total: 2.95% + 0.05%). Wage base = 66 2/3% of the average annual wage. 2025 base $41,800; 2027 base already announced at $45,400.

programs.name: Career Enhancement Program
programs.notes: Charged on UI taxable wages; not owed when the UI rate is 5.4%.

NV.agencyUnemployment: Nevada Department of Employment, Training and Rehabilitation
NV.deposit: No income tax withholding deposits. UI and CEP are paid quarterly with the quarterly contribution report; Modified Business Tax is paid quarterly with the MBT return, due the last day of the month after the quarter.

NV.notes: Confirm your unemployment rate with the Nevada Department of Employment, Training and Rehabilitation (DETR). Starting January 1, 2026 the Department of Taxation resumed matching MBT wages against NUCS-4072 wages. Modified Business Tax (1.17% general / 1.554% financial and mining of quarterly wages above $50,000, less health benefits) is a quarterly employer excise filed with the Department of Taxation; it is not calculated per paycheck.

NY.name: New York

single.label: Single or head of household (also married, withhold at single rate)

allowance.notes: IT-2104 allowances. Per-period exemption value: daily $3.85, weekly $19.25, biweekly $38.50, semimonthly $41.65, monthly $83.30, annual $1,000. Per-period deduction allowance (Table B): single daily $28.45 / weekly $142.30 / biweekly $284.60 / semimonthly $308.35 / monthly $616.70 / annual $7,400; married $30.60 / $152.90 / $305.80 / $331.25 / $662.50 / $7,950. 'Single' includes head of household and 'married, but withhold at higher single rate'. Employers that start from federal allowances can use Table D adjustments (based on a $4,300 federal allowance).

income.formula: NYS-50-T-NYS (1/26), Method II exact calculation: (1) net wages = wages - (deduction allowance + exemptions x exemption value) for the period (Table A); (2) annualize; (3) if annualized net wages are below $1,077,550 (single) or $2,155,350 (married), tax = column-5 base + (net - bracket start) x rate using the Annual Tax Rate Schedule (brackets listed with 'base'); (4) de-annualize; (5) otherwise use Method III: tax = annualized net wages x 10.45% (up to $5,000,000), 11.10% ($5,000,000-$25,000,000) or 11.70% ($25,000,000 and over), applied to the whole amount, then divide by pay periods. Example single weekly table: $0-$163 3.90%; $163-$225 $6.38 + 4.40%; $225-$267 $9.08 + 5.15%; $267-$1,551 $11.27 + 5.40%; $1,551-$1,862 $80.58 + 5.90%; $1,862-$2,070 $98.90 + 7.03%; $2,070-$3,032 $113.58 + 7.53%; $3,032-$4,142 $186.02 + 6.40%; $4,142-$5,104 $257.10 + 11.44%; $5,104-$20,722 $367.13 + 7.35%; Method III above.
income.deviations: Not a pure marginal schedule: the published 'base' amounts (column 5) contain rounding and benefit-recapture steps (rates go 7.53% -> 6.40% -> 11.44% -> 7.35%), so tax must be computed as base + rate x excess, not by summing marginal slices (summing differs by up to about $2/year). Very high earners switch to Method III, a flat rate on the whole annualized net wage. Married employees use their own schedule; head of household uses the single schedule. NYC and Yonkers taxes are computed separately (see localIncomeTaxes).
income.localTaxes: New York City resident tax (NYS-50-T-NYC): net wages = wages - deduction allowance ($5,000 single / $5,500 married annually) - $1,000 per exemption; annual schedule (same for single and married): 2.05% to $8,000; $164 + 2.80% over $8,000; $184 + 3.25% over $8,700; $388 + 3.95% over $15,000; $783 + 4.15% over $25,000; $2,236 + 4.25% over $60,000. NYC supplemental rate 4.25%. Yonkers resident: withhold 16.75% of the computed New York State withholding (supplemental 1.95975%). Yonkers nonresident earnings tax: 0.50% of annualized wages minus exclusion (no withholding under $4,000; exclusion $3,000 for $4,000-$10,000, $2,000 for $10,000-$20,000, $1,000 for $20,000-$30,000, none above), supplemental 0.50%.

sui.agency: New York State Department of Labor, Unemployment Insurance Division

The 0.075% Re-employment Service Fund (RSF) is reported on its own NYS-45 line (listed under other state taxes); totals including RSF are 4.1% new and 1.7%-9.5% experienced. programs.name: Disability Benefits Law
programs.notes: Employee 0.5% of wages, at most $0.60 per week (the weekly cap is applied to each paycheck times the weeks in its pay period). Collected for the DBL insurer.

programs.name: Paid Family Leave
programs.notes: 0.432% up to an annual maximum of $411.91; collected for the PFL insurer.

programs.name: Re-employment Service Fund
programs.notes: All contributory employers; NYS-45 line 5.

NY.agencyWithholding: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
NY.agencyUnemployment: New York State Department of Labor

NY.notes: 2026 tables reflect the rate cuts in Chapter 59 of the Laws of 2025 (Part A). Already-announced 2027 values: PFL 0.452% with annual cap $451.81 (NYSAWW $1,922.25). The 2027 UI wage base is not published yet. Rate notices are mailed in February. NYC and Yonkers income taxes are set up as local tax items. MCTMT is a quarterly employer tax by zone (not per paycheck).

OH.name: Ohio

allowance.notes: Exemptions claimed on Ohio IT 4. Per-period values in the percentage tables: weekly $12.50, biweekly $25.00, semimonthly $27.08, monthly $54.17, daily $2.50.

income.formula: Optional computer formula for payroll periods ending on or after August 1, 2026: TW = (pay per period x pay periods per year) - ($650 x exemptions). WD (annual) = TW x 1.600% if TW <= $26,050; (TW - $26,050) x 2.990% + $416.80 if TW <= $100,000; (TW - $100,000) x 3.400% + $2,627.91 above. Divide by pay periods. Percentage tables (same result): weekly 1.6% to $500.96, $8.02 + 2.99% to $1,923.08, $50.54 + 3.4% above; biweekly $1,001.92 / $3,846.15 ($16.03 / $101.07); semimonthly $1,085.42 / $4,166.67 ($17.37 / $109.50); monthly $2,170.83 / $8,333.33 ($34.73 / $218.99); daily $100.19 / $384.62 ($1.60 / $10.10).
income.deviations: Rates changed mid-year: tables effective October 1, 2025 applied to payroll periods ending before August 1, 2026 - TW <= $26,050 x 1.775%; $26,050-$100,000: (TW - $26,050) x 2.990% + $462.39; over $100,000: (TW - $100,000) x 3.640% + $2,673.50 (same $650 exemption). No filing status. Withholding rates exceed the 2026 statutory flat rate (2.75% over $26,050) by design. Supplemental (bonus) flat rate 2.75% from January 1, 2026 (3.5% in 2025).
income.localTaxes: Municipal income taxes in most Ohio cities and villages (work-location withholding, resident credits vary; administered by cities, RITA or CCA) and school district income tax for employees living in taxing school districts (traditional or earned-income base; employer withholds based on the IT 4 school district and files SD 101/SD 141).

sui.agency: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services (ODJFS), Office of Unemployment Insurance Operations
sui.notes: Construction new employer 5.7%. Mutualized rate 0.0% for 2026 (mutual account positive). Delinquency rate 12.6%. The 0.15% Technology and Customer Service Fee is separate (listed under other state taxes), so quoted totals are 2.85% new, 5.85% construction, 0.55%-10.25% experienced. Bills proposing a $9,500 wage base and a 0.14% employee tax (HB 321) are not reflected in the official 2026 rate table. 2025 base $9,000.

programs.name: Technology and Customer Service Fee
programs.notes: HB 96, 2026 and 2027; collected with quarterly UI contributions.

OH.agencyUnemployment: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services
OH.deposit: Based on combined Ohio + school district withholding in the 12-month look-back period ending June 30: $2,000 or less = quarterly (IT 501 due the last day of the month after the quarter); more than $2,000 and less than $84,000 = monthly (due the 15th of the following month); $84,000 or more = partial-weekly by EFT. Electronic filing and payment required (OH|TAX eServices).
OH.quarterlyReport: IT 501 Ohio Return for Income Tax Withheld (and SD 101 for school district tax) on the assigned schedule; UI: quarterly contribution and wage detail report filed electronically with ODJFS.
OH.annualReconciliation: IT 941 Annual Reconciliation of Income Tax Withheld (and SD 141 for school district tax), with W-2/1099 uploads, due January 31.
OH.notes: HB 96 (2025) made 2026 a flat 2.75% on nonbusiness income over $26,050 ($332 + 2.75% of the excess on the return). New withholding tables apply to payrolls ending on or after August 1, 2026. SerieX uses these tables for all 2026 paychecks. Municipal and school district income taxes are set up as local tax items.

OK.name: Oklahoma

single.label: Single; married but withhold at higher single rate

allowance.notes: OK-W-4 allowances ($1,000 personal exemption / pay periods): weekly $19.23, biweekly $38.46, semimonthly $41.67, monthly $83.33, quarterly $250, semiannual $500, annual $1,000, daily $3.85. 'Married, but withhold at higher single rate' uses the single table.

income.formula: Packet OW-2 (2026) percentage formula: (1) subtract allowances x the period allowance value from gross wages; (2) apply the period table for single or married; (3) round to the nearest whole dollar (under 50 cents down, 50 cents up). Annual table: single 0 to $10,100; 2.5% of excess over $10,100 to $11,250; $28.75 + 3.5% over $11,250 to $13,550; $109.25 + 4.5% over $13,550. Married 0 to $20,200; 2.5% to $22,500; $57.50 + 3.5% over $22,500 to $27,100; $218.50 + 4.5% over $27,100. Monthly single: 4.5% portion starts at $1,129 ($9.10 base); semimonthly single at $565 ($4.55); married monthly at $2,258 ($18.21).
income.deviations: Results rounded to the nearest whole dollar. The OW-2 does not publish a flat supplemental rate, so supplemental wages are added to regular wages; confirm with the Oklahoma Tax Commission (OTC) before using a flat rate.

sui.agency: Oklahoma Employment Security Commission (OESC)
sui.notes: S.B. 911 (2025) lowered the wage-base percentage and the rate table. 2025: base $28,200, rates 0.3%-9.2%. New employers keep 1.5% until four quarters of experience. Already announced for 2027: wage base $24,400, rates 0.1%-5.5% (OESC contribution rates page).

OK.deposit: Withholding of $500 or less per quarter: pay quarterly with WTH-10001 by the 20th of the month after the quarter. More than $500 per quarter: pay monthly by the 20th of the following month (coupon WTH-10004 or OkTAP). Average of $10,000 or more per month in the previous fiscal year: pay on the federal semiweekly schedule. Electronic payment required at $5,000 or more per month.
OK.quarterlyReport: WTH-10001 Oklahoma Quarterly Wage Withholding Tax Return (due the 20th after the quarter); UI: OES-3 Employer's Quarterly Contribution and Wage Report via the OESC Employer Portal (due the last day of the month after the quarter).
OK.annualReconciliation: W-2s and W-3 submitted to the OTC through OkTAP (EFW2 format) by January 31.
OK.notes: 2026 tables reflect HB 2764 (2025): 0% on the first $3,750 (single) / $7,500 (married) of taxable income, 2.5%, 3.5%, then 4.5% top rate; the tables embed a $6,350 / $12,700 standard deduction (zero band $10,100 / $20,200). There is no published supplemental flat rate, so supplemental wages are added to regular wages.

OR.name: Oregon

married_single.label: Married, but withhold at higher single rate

allowance.notes: OR-W-4 allowances; $263 exemption credit per allowance, subtracted after the tax computation. Allowances are set to 0 when a single employee's annual wages exceed $100,000 or a married employee's exceed $200,000. 'Single' table = single or head of household with fewer than 3 allowances; 'married' table = married, or single with 3 or more allowances.

income.formula: Oregon Withholding Tax Formulas 150-206-436 (effective January 1, 2026), annual computer formula, then divide by pay periods: BASE = annual wages - annual federal income tax withheld (capped at $8,750; phased out for high wages) - standard deduction ($2,910 single table / $5,820 married table). Annual wages under $50,000: single table WH = 263 + BASE x 4.75% (BASE to $4,550); 479 + (BASE - 4,550) x 6.75% (to $11,400); 941 + (BASE - 11,400) x 8.75% (to $50,000); married table WH = 263 + BASE x 4.75% (to $9,100); 695 + (BASE - 9,100) x 6.75% (to $22,800); 1,620 + (BASE - 22,800) x 8.75%. Then subtract 263 x allowances. Annual wages $50,000 or more: single WH = 678 + (BASE - 11,400) x 8.75% (BASE to $125,000), 10,618 + (BASE - 125,000) x 9.9% above; married WH = 1,357 + (BASE - 22,800) x 8.75% (to $250,000), 21,237 + (BASE - 250,000) x 9.9% above; minus 263 x allowances. Federal-tax cap phase-out - single-table (also married-withholding-at-single-rate and single with 3+ allowances): $8,750 for wages $50,000-<$125,000, $7,000 <$130,000, $5,250 <$135,000, $3,500 <$140,000, $1,750 <$145,000, $0 at $145,000+; married: $8,750 to <$250,000, $7,000 <$260,000, $5,250 <$270,000, $3,500 <$280,000, $1,750 <$290,000, $0 at $290,000+. Negative result = 0. Rounding to the nearest dollar optional.
income.deviations: Subtracts the employee's federal income tax withholding (capped and phased out) before the brackets; adds a $263 constant (equal to one exemption credit) to the computed tax when annual wages are under $50,000 (the bracket bases already include it, see the 263/479/941 constants) but not at $50,000 and over; allowances zeroed above $100,000 single / $200,000 married; the married table also applies to single employees with 3+ allowances. Employees with no withholding statement must be withheld at a flat 8%. The FAQ and worked example in the booklet still quote stale figures ($8,500 cap, $256 credit); the formula tables ($8,750, $263) were used.
income.localTaxes: Portland-area personal income taxes administered by the City of Portland Revenue Division: Metro Supportive Housing Services (SHS) tax and Multnomah County Preschool for All (PFA) tax on taxable income above high-income thresholds, with employer withholding/opt-in-opt-out rules; confirm current rates and thresholds with the City of Portland Revenue Division. No other local income taxes.

sui.agency: Oregon Employment Department (OED)
sui.notes: Tax Schedule 3 for 2026 (same as 2025). New employers (less than 12 months of payroll) 2.4%. Rates include a Special Payroll Tax Offset of 0.135% (Q1 and Q2 2026) that is part of the assigned rate, not an extra charge. 2025 wage base $54,300.

programs.name: Statewide Transit Tax
programs.notes: 0.1% of all wages, no cap.

programs.name: Paid Leave Oregon
programs.notes: 1% total up to $184,500; employer 0.4% only for employers with 25+ employees (set 0 in State settings otherwise).

OR.deposit: Same due dates as federal deposits: federal liability under $2,500 for the quarter = pay with the quarterly report; $50,000 or less in the lookback period = monthly by the 15th of the following month; more than $50,000 = semiweekly; $100,000 in a single pay period = next banking day. New businesses deposit monthly. EFT required when EFTPS is required federally.
OR.quarterlyReport: Form OQ Oregon Quarterly Tax Report (Oregon Combined Payroll Tax Report: withholding, UI, TriMet, Lane Transit, STT, Paid Leave and WBF); household employers may file annual Form OA, agricultural employers Form WA.
OR.annualReconciliation: Form WR Oregon Annual Withholding Tax Reconciliation Report with W-2s, due January 31.
OR.notes: Already announced for 2027 (Oregon DCBS): Workers' Benefit Fund 2.4 cents per hour (2.2 cents assessment + 0.2 cent BOLI Expense Fund). 2025 WBF was 2.0 cents; 2025 Paid Leave wage base $176,100. Workers' Benefit Fund (1.8 cents per hour, half from the employee) is per hour worked, not a wage percentage. TriMet (0.8237%) and Lane Transit (0.80%) employer payroll taxes apply only to work inside those districts: set them up as local tax items.

PA.name: Pennsylvania

allowance.notes: No withholding allowances, no standard deduction and no filing status.

income.stateForm: none (REV-419 Employee's Nonwithholding Application Certificate for reciprocity-state residents and eligibility-for-forgiveness cases)
income.formula: Withhold a flat 3.07% of PA-taxable compensation for resident and nonresident employees earning income in Pennsylvania. No allowances, no deduction, no annualization needed.
income.deviations: PA-taxable compensation follows Pennsylvania's own definition, which can differ from federal Box 1 wages (some pre-tax deductions are treated differently; confirm with the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue). Residents of Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, Ohio, Virginia and West Virginia are exempt under reciprocity when they file REV-419.
income.localTaxes: Local Earned Income Tax (Act 32): withhold the higher of the employee's resident total EIT rate or the work-location nonresident EIT rate (rates vary by municipality/school district; obtain from the DCED PSD lookup) and remit to the work-location tax collector. Local Services Tax (LST) up to $52 per year (prorated per pay period; low-income exemption may apply). Philadelphia (outside Act 32) Wage Tax: 3.735% residents / 3.425% nonresidents for wages paid after June 30, 2026 (3.74% / 3.43% January 1-June 30, 2026), remitted to the City of Philadelphia.

sui.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Labor & Industry, Office of Unemployment Compensation Tax Services
sui.notes: New employer rates: 3.8220% non-construction, 10.5924% construction (unchanged since 2023). Experienced non-delinquent totals 1.419%-10.3734% including the 9.2% surcharge adjustment and the 0.60% additional contributions tax; delinquent employers 4.695%-14.4684%. Employee UC withholding 0.07% of total gross wages with no wage cap. Static $10,000 employer wage base.

PA.deposit: Under $300 per quarter: quarterly, due the last day of April, July, October and January. $300-$999 per quarter: monthly, due the 15th of the following month. $1,000-$4,999.99 per quarter: semimonthly, due within three banking days after the semimonthly period. $5,000 or more per quarter ($20,000 per year): semiweekly, due the Wednesday after Wednesday-Friday paydays and the Friday after Saturday-Tuesday paydays. File and pay through myPATH.

PA.annualReconciliation: REV-1667 Annual Withholding Reconciliation Statement (W-2 transmittal) with W-2s, due January 31.
PA.notes: Philadelphia employer wage tax payments: quarterly under $350/month, monthly $350-$16,000/month, semimonthly or weekly at $16,000+/month; quarterly returns due the last day of the month after the quarter. PA UC rates for 2026 were unchanged from 2025. Employee UC withholding 0.07% applies to total wages with no cap (the employee wage base of $1,000,000,000 shown means no cap). Local Earned Income Tax, LST and Philadelphia wage tax are set up as local tax items.

RI.name: Rhode Island

allowance.notes: One withholding exemption = $1,000 per year (weekly $19.23, biweekly $38.46, semimonthly $41.67, monthly $83.33, quarterly $250, semiannual $500, daily/misc $3.85). The exemption value becomes $0 when wages for the period exceed the phase-out threshold: annual $290,800 (weekly $5,592.31, biweekly $11,184.62, semimonthly $12,116.67, monthly $24,233.33, quarterly $72,700, semiannual $145,400, daily $1,118.46). Allowances come from Form RI W-4 line 1 (capped at 10 on the worksheet line 1E).

income.formula: Official 2026 percentage method (wages paid on or after Jan 1, 2026), same table for ALL filing statuses: (1) Wages = wages subject to federal income tax withholding for the period. (2) Exemption amount = number of RI W-4 exemptions x per-period exemption value ($1,000/yr; weekly $19.23; biweekly $38.46; semimonthly $41.67; monthly $83.33; quarterly $250; semiannual $500; daily $3.85); if period wages exceed the period phase-out threshold (annual $290,800; weekly $5,592.31; biweekly $11,184.62; semimonthly $12,116.67; monthly $24,233.33) the exemption amount is $0. (3) Taxable = wages - exemption amount. (4) Apply the period table. Annual table: $0-$82,050: 3.75%; $82,050-$186,450: $3,076.88 + 4.75% of excess over $82,050; over $186,450: $8,035.88 + 5.99% of excess over $186,450. Per-period tables are the annual table divided by periods and rounded (weekly breakpoints $1,578/$3,586, base amounts $59.18/$154.56; biweekly $3,156/$7,171, $118.35/$309.06; semimonthly $3,419/$7,769, $128.21/$334.84; monthly $6,838/$15,538, $256.43/$669.68). (5) Add any additional amount from RI W-4 line 2. Supplemental wages paid separately: either aggregate method or flat 5.99%.
income.deviations: Same as the generic model (annualize -> minus allowances x $1,000 -> brackets -> de-annualize) EXCEPT the exemption value drops to $0 when annualized wages exceed $290,800 (cliff, not a gradual phase-out). Official per-period tables use rounded breakpoints, so annualizing can differ by a few cents from the published per-period table.

sui.agency: Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training (DLT), Employer Tax Unit
sui.notes: 2026 Tax Schedule F. All three rates INCLUDE the 0.21% Job Development Assessment (JDA): new employer = 1.00% employment security + 0.21% JDA = 1.21%; experienced = 0.69%-9.19% employment security + 0.21% JDA = 0.90%-9.40%. Do not add JDA again. Employers at the highest rate (9.19% ES, i.e. 9.40% total) use a $32,300 wage base instead of $30,800. JDA and TDI are reported and paid with UI on Form TX-17. 2025: wage base $29,800 (highest-rate employers $1,500 higher), Schedule G, new employer rate 1.21% (unchanged for 2026).

programs.name: Temporary Disability / Caregiver Insurance
programs.notes: Employee-paid 1.1% up to $100,000; workers aged 14 and 15 are exempt.

RI.agencyUnemployment: Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training
RI.deposit: Weekly (by next banking day after the Sun-Sat week, generally Monday, electronically) if $600+ withheld in a calendar month; monthly (by the 20th of the following month with Form WTM/RI-941M; quarter-end months reported on RI-941 by the last day of the following month) if $50-$599 per month (electronic if $200+ per month); quarterly (RI-941 by last day of month after quarter) if under $50 per month. Electronic filing/payment also mandatory if total RI tax liability >= $5,000/yr or gross income > $100,000.
RI.quarterlyReport: Withholding: RI-941 Employer's Quarterly Tax Return and Reconciliation (Division of Taxation). UI/JDA/TDI: TX-17 Quarterly Tax and Wage Report (DLT).
RI.annualReconciliation: RI-W3 Transmittal of Wage and Tax Statements, due January 31
RI.notes: 2025 withholding values (for corrections): annual brackets 3.75% to $79,900; $2,996.25 + 4.75% to $181,650; $7,829.38 + 5.99% over $181,650; exemption $1,000; exemption becomes $0 above $283,250 annual wages; supplemental 5.99%. 2027 values not yet announced (RI normally publishes withholding tables in late fall and DLT rates in December). UI rates include the 0.21% Job Development Assessment.

SC.name: South Carolina

allowance.notes: $5,000 per allowance claimed on the SC W-4 (per period: monthly $416.67, semimonthly $208.33, biweekly $192.31, weekly $96.15). No filing statuses in the SC formula.

income.formula: SCDOR WH-1603F (Rev. 11/4/25), 2026: (1) Annualize gross wages (period wages x pay periods). (2) If 1 or more allowances: subtract $5,000 x allowances AND subtract a standard deduction of 10% of annual gross wages, capped at $7,500. If 0 allowances: subtract nothing (no allowance, no standard deduction). (3) Tax on annual taxable income: $0-$3,640: 0%; $3,640-$18,230: 3% of amount over $3,640 (equivalently 3% x income - $109.20); $18,230 and over: $437.70 + 6.0% of amount over $18,230 (equivalently 6% x income - $656.10). (4) Divide annual tax by pay periods. (5) Add any additional amount requested on SC W-4. Per-period constants: max standard deduction monthly $625.00, semimonthly $312.50, biweekly $288.46, weekly $144.23; max tax in first bracket annual $437.70 (monthly $36.48, semimonthly $18.24, biweekly $16.83, weekly $8.42).
income.deviations: Standard deduction is 10% of annualized gross wages (cap $7,500) and applies only when at least one allowance is claimed; zero allowances means no standard deduction at all. No filing-status tables. SC does not publish a flat supplemental rate in WH-1603F; use the aggregate (combine with regular wages) approach.

sui.agency: South Carolina Department of Employment and Workforce (DEW)
sui.notes: 2026 rates INCLUDE the 0.06% Departmental Administrative Contingency Assessment (DACA); solvency surcharge is 0.00% for 2026. New employers = rate class 30: 1.00% base + 0.06% DACA = 1.06% (DEW press release quotes the 1.0% base). Experienced classes 1-20 run 0.06% (class 1) to 5.46% (class 20). Wage base unchanged at $14,000 for 2025 and 2026.

SC.agencyUnemployment: South Carolina Department of Employment and Workforce
SC.deposit: Resident withholding agents pay with the same frequency as their federal deposits (monthly or semiweekly). Must file and pay electronically (MyDORWAY) if withholding $15,000+ per quarter or making 24+ payments a year. Quarterly returns due by the last day of the month after the quarter.
SC.quarterlyReport: Withholding: WH-1605 (quarters 1-3). UI: UCE-120 Employer Quarterly Contribution and Wage Report (DEW).
SC.annualReconciliation: WH-1606 (4th quarter return / annual reconciliation), due January 31, with W-2s uploaded to SCDOR
SC.notes: IMPORTANT: Act 110 of 2026 (H.4216, signed March 30, 2026) changed 2026 individual income tax rates to 1.99% on taxable income under $30,000 and (5.21% x income) - $966 at $30,000+, retroactive to tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2025, and directs SCDOR to adjust withholding tables. As of SCDOR Information Letter 26-20 (Aug 31, 2026) no revised withholding tables had been issued, so the 2026 WH-1603F (Rev. 11/4/25) shown is still the official employer formula. Check dor.sc.gov/withholding for revised tables. Act 110 also provides top-rate cuts starting tax year 2027 if a revenue trigger is met. 2025 withholding values (for corrections): $4,860 per allowance; standard deduction 10% capped at $7,300; 0% to $3,560; 3% from $3,560 to $17,830; $428.10 + 6.2% over $17,830 (subtraction method 6.2% - $677.36). No supplemental flat rate in WH-1603F (aggregate). Act 110 of 2026 rate cut not yet reflected in official withholding tables.

SD.name: South Dakota

income.formula: No state individual income tax; no state withholding on wages.

sui.notes: Rates here are the Reemployment Assistance (RA) contribution only; the Investment Fee and Administrative Fee are listed under other state taxes. New non-construction employer: 1.20% in year 1, 1.00% in years 2-3 (if account balance positive); new construction employer: 6.00% year 1, 3.00% years 2-3. New-employer total including the 0.55% investment fee = 1.75% (year 1 non-construction). Experienced contribution rates for wages paid on/after Jan 1, 2026 (SDCL 61-5-25.7): 0.00% (reserve ratio 2.25%+) up to 9.39% (Schedule A), 9.24% (Schedule B) or 8.52% (Schedule C) for reserve ratio below -7.00%; the schedule in force depends on the trust fund level (confirm which schedule applies for 2026 with the South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation). Wage base $15,000 since 2015.

programs.notes: 0.55% for new employers (years 1-3); experience-rated employers 0.00%-0.53% by reserve ratio.

programs.name: Administrative Fee
programs.notes: Only employers eligible for experience rating (not new employers): set the rate to 0 in State settings when not owed.

SD.agencyUnemployment: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation
SD.deposit: No state income tax withholding. RA contributions and fees are paid quarterly with the quarterly report (due by the last day of the month after the quarter).
SD.quarterlyReport: Quarterly Reemployment Assistance contribution and wage report, filed online with DLR
SD.notes: No state disability or paid leave program. Wage base is fixed at $15,000 (also 2025 and expected 2027 unless the law changes).

TN.name: Tennessee

income.formula: No state income tax on wages; no state withholding.

sui.agency: Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development (TDLWD), Employment Security / Employer Accounts
sui.notes: Premium Rate Table 6 is in effect for both Jan 1, 2026 and Jul 1, 2026 periods (Tennessee sets the table semiannually). Table 6: positive-balance employers 0.01%-2.30%, negative-balance employers 5.00%-10.00%. New employer rate 2.7% (statute: unless the employer's 2-digit NAICS sector has a reserve ratio below 0%, in which case the sector rate applies) until 36 consecutive months of experience. Experience rates are effective for a four-quarter year beginning July 1. Wage base $7,000 since 2018.
