TN.notes: No state disability or paid leave program. 2025 identical: wage base $7,000, Table 6, new employer 2.7%.

TX.name: Texas

income.formula: No state individual income tax; no state withholding.

sui.agency: Texas Workforce Commission (TWC)
sui.notes: Effective tax rate = General Tax Rate (benefit ratio x 2026 replenishment ratio 1.20%) + Replenishment Tax Rate 0.21% (already reduced by 0.10% to offset ETIA) + Obligation Assessment 0.01% + Deficit Tax Rate (0.00% for 2026; confirm on your TWC rate notice) + Employment and Training Investment Assessment (ETIA) 0.10%. The 0.32%-6.32% range and the 2.70% new-employer (entry-level) rate are TOTAL effective rates including ETIA; do not add ETIA again (ETIA is shown separately on the C-3 but is not a FUTA-creditable contribution). Entry-level rate = higher of NAICS industry average or 2.70%; for 2026 it is 2.70% for all industry groups with no exceptions. 2026 average rate 1.20%. Wage base fixed by statute at $9,000.

TX.deposit: No state income tax withholding. UI tax paid quarterly with Form C-3 (due by the last day of the month after the quarter).
TX.quarterlyReport: Form C-3 Employer's Quarterly Report (TWC), filed via Unemployment Tax Services
TX.notes: No state disability or paid leave program. 2025: wage base $9,000; 2025 RTR was 0.15% (TWC discussion paper); confirm 2025 minimum and maximum rates with the Texas Workforce Commission (TWC).

UT.name: Utah

single.label: Single (single, married filing separately, head of household)

allowance.notes: No per-allowance amounts. Instead a filing-status 'base allowance' credit ($485 single / $970 married per year) is reduced by 1.3% of annual wages above $9,348 (single) / $18,696 (married), not below zero. Federal W-4 Step 1(c): married filing jointly -> married schedule; single, married filing separately and head of household -> single schedule. No federal W-4 on file: flat 4.45% with no base allowance.

income.formula: Utah Pub 14 (Rev. 4/26), for pay periods beginning on or after June 1, 2026: (1) Utah taxable wages = wages subject to federal income tax withholding (no subtraction for W-4 allowances/adjustments). (2) Gross tax = 4.45% x wages. (3) Allowance reduction = 1.3% x (wages - threshold), not less than 0; threshold annual $9,348 single / $18,696 married. (4) Net allowance = base allowance ($485 single / $970 married annual) - reduction, not less than 0. (5) Withholding = gross tax - net allowance, not less than 0. Pub 14 per-period schedules use rounded constants (base allowance / threshold): weekly S $9/$180, M $19/$360; biweekly S $19/$360, M $37/$719; semimonthly S $20/$390, M $40/$779; monthly S $40/$779, M $81/$1,558; quarterly S $121/$2,337, M $243/$4,674; semiannual S $243/$4,674, M $485/$9,348; annual S $485/$9,348, M $970/$18,696; daily S $2/$36, M $4/$72. Pub 14 worked examples round each line to whole dollars. For pay periods beginning Jan 1 - May 31, 2026 the prior schedules applied: 4.5%, base allowance $450 single / $900 married, thresholds $9,107 / $18,213 (annual).
income.deviations: Flat rate with a phase-out credit (base allowance reduced by 1.3% of wages over a threshold) rather than per-allowance deductions/credits; status comes from federal W-4; employees without a W-4 get no base allowance. Official per-period schedules use rounded constants, so annualizing can differ slightly. Mid-year change: new rate/allowances only for pay periods beginning on/after June 1, 2026 (SB 60 cut is retroactive to Jan 1 for the annual return, but withholding was not retro-adjusted). No flat supplemental rate is published in Pub 14.

sui.agency: Utah Department of Workforce Services (DWS), Unemployment Insurance
sui.notes: New employers are assigned a rate from the 2-year average benefit ratio of their industry (not less than 1% x reserve factor + social cost), so there is no single new-employer rate; new out-of-state contractors get the maximum 7.1%. Overall rate = benefit ratio x reserve factor (1.10 for 2026) + social cost. 2026 min 0.1%, max 7.1%; a 1.0% delinquency surcharge may be added. 2025 wage base $48,900.

UT.deposit: Utah does not follow federal deposit schedules. Quarterly return and payment (by last day of month after quarter) if under $1,000 withheld per month; quarterly return with monthly payments (by last day of following month) if $1,000+ per month; annual (by Jan 31) for Schedule H/Form 944 household employers. All returns must be filed electronically at tap.utah.gov.
UT.quarterlyReport: Withholding: TC-941 Utah Withholding Return (electronic). UI: Form 3 Employer's Contribution Report with Form 3H Quarterly Wage List (DWS).
UT.annualReconciliation: Annual withholding reconciliation filed electronically with all W-2/1099s by January 31 (combined with the 4th-quarter or annual withholding return)
UT.notes: Mid-year change: S.B. 60 (2026) cut the rate from 4.5% to 4.45% retroactive to Jan 1, 2026; revised Pub 14 applies to pay periods beginning on or after June 1, 2026. 2025 values (and Jan-May 2026 withholding): 4.5%, $450/$900 base allowance, thresholds $9,107 single / $18,213 married, 1.3% reduction rate. No state disability or paid leave program. SerieX uses the rates for pay periods beginning on or after June 1, 2026 for all 2026 paychecks. New employers get an industry rate, so no new employer rate is filled in: enter the rate the Utah Department of Workforce Services (DWS) assigned you in State settings.

VA.name: Virginia

allowance.notes: E1 = personal and dependent exemptions from Form VA-4 line 1(a), $930 each. E2 = age-65-and-over and blind exemptions from VA-4 line 1(b), $800 each. No VA-4 on file: withhold as if no exemptions. The $8,750 standard deduction is the same for every employee regardless of marital status.

income.formula: Virginia Tax employer formula (effective for wages paid after July 1, 2025; still current per guide Rev. 10/26): (1) T = (G x P) - [$8,750 + (E1 x $930) + (E2 x $800)], where G = gross pay for the period, P = pay periods per year. (2) W = annual tax: T not over $3,000: 2% of T; $3,000-$5,000: $60 + 3% of excess over $3,000; $5,000-$17,000: $120 + 5% of excess over $5,000; over $17,000: $720 + 5.75% of excess over $17,000. (3) Withholding per period = W / P. Add any additional amount on VA-4 line 2. Supplemental wages paid separately: aggregate method (tax on regular+supplemental minus tax on regular) or, if tax was withheld from regular wages, a flat 5.75% without exemptions.
income.deviations: Fits the generic model except there are two exemption types with different values ($930 personal/dependent and $800 age/blind). Otherwise annualize -> minus $8,750 -> minus exemptions -> brackets -> divide by periods. Wage-bracket tables in the guide are approximate; the formula is exact.

sui.agency: Virginia Employment Commission (VEC)
sui.notes: These are BASE tax rates (VEC: new employers 2.5% base 'plus add-ons'; experienced base rates 0.1%-6.2%). Add-ons charged to all employers and included in the total rate on the VEC rate notice: a pool cost charge (computed yearly; 0.03% on recent notices) and a 0.2% fund building charge that applies only when the trust fund balance factor is 50% or less (Va. Code 60.2-533 C). The 2026 add-ons are usually quoted as 0.03% + 0.20% (about 2.73% total for new employers); use the total on your VEC rate notice. Wage base $8,000 (unchanged).

VA.deposit: Assigned by Virginia Tax: quarterly (average monthly liability under $100; VA-5 and payment by last day of month after quarter); monthly ($100-$999 per month; VA-5 and payment by the 25th of the following month); semi-weekly ($1,000+ per month; payment with VA-15 within 3 banking days after each federal semi-weekly cutoff, plus quarterly VA-16 reconciliation by last day of month after quarter). Equivalent quarterly thresholds: < $300, $300-$2,999, $3,000+.
VA.quarterlyReport: Withholding: VA-5 (monthly/quarterly filers) or VA-16 (semi-weekly filers). UI: VEC FC-20 Employer's Quarterly Tax Report and FC-21 Employer's Quarterly Payroll Report.
VA.annualReconciliation: VA-6 Employer's Annual or Final Summary of Virginia Income Tax Withheld (VA-6H for household employers), due January 31 with W-2s filed electronically
VA.notes: 2025 values (for corrections): wages paid after July 1, 2025 used the same $8,750 formula; wages paid before then used $8,500 (otherwise identical). 2027 (announced in law): the 2026 General Assembly amended Va. Code 58.1-322.03 so the standard deduction is $9,200 single / $18,400 married for tax year 2027 and $9,300 / $18,600 for 2028-2029; Virginia Tax has not yet published 2027 withholding tables (the guide Rev. 10/26 still mentions the older sunset language). Paid Family and Medical Leave (HB 1207/SB 2, signed 2026): VEC sets the contribution rate by Oct 1, 2027; payroll contributions start April 1, 2028 (50/50 employer/employee; employers with 10 or fewer employees remit only the employee share), on wages up to the Social Security wage base. No contributions in 2026 or 2027. Daily payrolls are annualized with 300 days (Virginia formula pay period conversion: daily = 300).

VT.name: Vermont

single.label: Single, head of household, or married but withhold at single rate

allowance.notes: One allowance = $5,400/yr (weekly $103.85, biweekly $207.69, semimonthly $225.00, monthly $450.00, quarterly $1,350, daily $20.77). Allowances and status from Form W-4VT. Civil union / civil marriage partners use the married table. Single table also used for head of household and 'married but withhold at higher single rate'.

income.formula: GB-1210-2026 percentage method (effective Jan 1 - Dec 31, 2026): (1) Subtract (allowances x per-period allowance value) from period wages. (2) Apply the single or married table. Annual single: $0-$3,925: $0; $3,925-$54,675: 3.35% of excess over $3,925; $54,675-$126,775: $1,700.13 + 6.60% over $54,675; $126,775-$260,225: $6,458.73 + 7.60% over $126,775; over $260,225: $16,600.93 + 8.75% over $260,225. Annual married: $0-$11,775: $0; $11,775-$96,475: 3.35% over $11,775; $96,475-$216,525: $2,837.45 + 6.60% over $96,475; $216,525-$323,825: $10,760.75 + 7.60% over $216,525; over $323,825: $18,915.55 + 8.75% over $323,825. Per-period tables (weekly/biweekly/semimonthly/monthly/quarterly/daily) are the annual table divided and rounded, e.g. weekly single breakpoints $75/$1,051/$2,438/$5,004, married $226/$1,855/$4,164/$6,227. (3) Add extra withholding from W-4VT. If no W-4VT is on file the employer may use the federal W-4; if that W-4 requests extra federal withholding per period, increase Vermont withholding by 30% of the extra federal amount.
income.deviations: Fits the generic model (the 0% first bracket acts as the standard deduction). Minor: official per-period tables have rounded breakpoints. No flat supplemental rate: supplemental/periodic payments use the tables; nonperiodic payments may be estimated at 30% of federal withholding; payments from a non-qualified deferred compensation plan are withheld at 6%.

sui.agency: Vermont Department of Labor (VDOL), Unemployment Insurance
sui.notes: Wage base $15,400 for calendar 2026 (2025: $14,800). Rates run on a July 1 - June 30 rate year; five statutory schedules (21 V.S.A. 1326) of 21 classes each: Schedule 1 0.4%-5.4% ... Schedule 5 1.3%-8.4%. The range shown is Schedule 1 (0.4%-5.4%); confirm the schedule for the rate year beginning July 1, 2026 with the Vermont Department of Labor (VDOL). New employer rate for most employers is 1.0% (VDOL: 'Beginning July 1, 2026'); out-of-state construction new employers get industry averages: NAICS 236 1.9%, 237 4.0%, 238 2.7%.

programs.name: Child Care Contribution
programs.notes: 0.44% of wages subject to VT withholding; employer may withhold up to 0.11% (if not withheld set employee 0 and employer 0.44 in State settings).

VT.deposit: Payment frequency generally mirrors the federal frequency: semiweekly (Wed/Thu/Fri pay dates due following Wednesday; other pay dates due following Friday); monthly (by the 25th of the following month; January due Feb 23); quarterly (paid with WHT-436). All filers file WHT-436 Quarterly Withholding Reconciliation by the 25th of the month after each quarter. CCC follows the same schedule.
VT.quarterlyReport: Withholding/CCC/Health Care: WHT-436 Quarterly Withholding Reconciliation (Department of Taxes). UI: C-101 Employer's Quarterly Wage and Contribution Report (VDOL, filed online).
VT.annualReconciliation: WHT-434 Annual Withholding Reconciliation, due January 31 (transmits W-2/1099; electronic if 10+ forms)
VT.notes: 2025 withholding values (for corrections): allowance $5,300; annual single 0% to $3,825, 3.35% to $53,225, $1,654.90 + 6.60% to $123,525, $6,294.70 + 7.60% to $253,525, $16,174.70 + 8.75% above; married 0% to $11,475, 3.35% to $93,975, $2,763.75 + 6.60% to $210,925, $10,482.45 + 7.60% to $315,475, $18,428.25 + 8.75% above. The 2027 UI wage base is not announced yet (VDOL announced the 2026 base on Oct 6, 2025). No state disability insurance; Vermont's voluntary paid family leave program has no mandatory payroll contribution. Health Care Fund Contribution Assessment is per uncovered FTE per quarter (not a wage percentage).

WA.name: Washington

income.formula: No state income tax on wages; no state withholding.
income.localTaxes: none (Seattle's payroll expense tax is an employer business tax on large payrolls, not withheld from wages)

sui.agency: Washington State Employment Security Department (ESD)
sui.notes: Rates shown are the total UI rate (experience rate + graduated social cost rate) for qualified employers, 40 rate classes: class 1 = 0.24% (0.00 + 0.24) to class 40 = 6.00% (capped). The Employment Administration Fund (EAF) is listed separately under other state taxes; ESD's 'Total' column including EAF is 0.27%-6.02%. Delinquent employers pay +0.5% to +2.0% (up to 8.12% UI / 8.15% with EAF). New employers: 115% of the average rate for their industry for 2026, minimum 1.0% (federal floor), until 2.5-3 years in business; no single rate. 2025 wage base $72,800. 2027 wage base announced: $82,000.

programs.name: Paid Family and Medical Leave
programs.notes: 1.13% total premium. Employer share only for employers with 50 or more WA employees (set 0 in State settings otherwise).

programs.name: WA Cares Fund
programs.notes: 0.58% of all wages, no cap; employees with an approved exemption are not charged.

programs.name: Employment Administration Fund
programs.notes: Added to the UI rate on the same taxable wages (0.02% for rate class 40).

WA.deposit: No state income tax withholding. UI, PFML and WA Cares premiums are paid quarterly with the quarterly reports (due by the last day of the month after the quarter). L&I premiums quarterly.
WA.quarterlyReport: ESD Quarterly Tax and Wage Report (UI); ESD Paid Leave/WA Cares quarterly report; L&I Quarterly Report for Industrial Insurance
WA.notes: 2027 already announced: UI wage base $82,000; PFML 1.20% (70.7% employee / 29.3% employer). Workers' compensation (L&I) is charged per hour worked by risk class and is not calculated as a wage percentage. New employers pay 115% of their industry average rate (minimum 1.0%), so no new employer rate is filled in: enter the rate the Employment Security Department (ESD) assigned you in State settings.

WI.name: Wisconsin

married_single.label: Married, but withhold at higher single rate

allowance.notes: $400 per exemption claimed on Form WT-4. WT-4 statuses: Single; Married; Married but withhold at higher single rate (uses single). No head-of-household schedule. Federal W-4 cannot be used.

income.formula: Publication W-166 (1/26) 'Alternate Method' (formula in effect since Jan 1, 2022, unchanged for 2026): (a) Annual gross = period wage x periods. (b) Subtract the deduction amount: SINGLE: gross < $17,780 -> $6,702; gross >= $73,630 -> $0; otherwise $6,702 - 0.12 x (gross - $17,780). MARRIED: gross < $25,727 -> $9,461; gross >= $73,032 -> $0; otherwise $9,461 - 0.20 x (gross - $25,727). (c) Subtract $400 x exemptions -> annual net wage. (d) Tax: not over $12,760: 3.54%; $12,760-$25,520: $451.70 + 4.65% over $12,760; $25,520-$280,950: $1,045.04 + 5.30% over $25,520; over $280,950: $14,582.83 + 7.65% over $280,950. (e) Divide by periods. Add any additional amount on WT-4. Supplemental wages: aggregate with regular wages, or apply the approved flat percentage based on the employee's estimated annual gross salary: under $12,760: 3.54%; $12,760-$25,520: 4.65%; $25,520-$280,950: 5.30%; $280,950 and over: 7.65%.
income.deviations: The standard deduction slides down with annual gross wages (12% single / 20% married phase-out) instead of being fixed; brackets are the same for single and married. Supplemental flat rate depends on estimated annual salary (no single rate). Withholding-table rates (3.54/4.65/5.30/7.65) differ from return rates (3.50/4.40/5.30/7.65) by design.

sui.agency: Wisconsin Department of Workforce Development (DWD), Unemployment Insurance Division
sui.notes: Schedule D in effect for 2026 (Wis. Stat. 108.18). Rates are basic + solvency. New employers: 3.05% if taxable payroll under $500,000 (2.50 + 0.55), 3.25% if $500,000 or more (2.50 + 0.75); new construction employers 2.50% / 2.70%. Experienced range: payroll < $500,000: 0.00%-12.00%; payroll >= $500,000: 0.05%-12.00%. 2025: construction new employer 2.90%/3.10%, others 3.05%/3.25%, wage base $14,000. 2027 announced: Schedule D again, wage base $14,000, same new-employer rates (3.05/3.25; construction 2.50/2.70).

WI.deposit: DOR assigns a filing frequency: semi-monthly (pay dates 1st-15th due last day of the month; 16th-end due 15th of next month), monthly or quarterly (WT-6 deposit report due last day of month after the period), or annual (no WT-6; reported on WT-7). A WT-6 must be filed each period even with no tax.
WI.quarterlyReport: Withholding: WT-6 Withholding Tax Deposit Report. UI: UCT-101-E Quarterly Contribution Report and UC-7823-E Quarterly Wage Report (DWD).
WI.annualReconciliation: WT-7 Employer's Annual Reconciliation of Wisconsin Income Tax Withheld, due January 31 (with W-2s)
WI.notes: 2025 withholding formula identical to 2026. No state disability or paid leave program. W-166 does not state the default when no WT-4 is furnished; common practice is single with 0 exemptions. Supplemental wages: aggregate with regular wages (the optional flat rate depends on estimated annual salary).

WV.name: West Virginia

two_earner.label: Two earner / two or more jobs (default)

allowance.notes: $2,000 per exemption on WV/IT-104 (weekly $38.46, biweekly $76.92, semimonthly $83.33, monthly $166.67, daily $7.66). 'two_earner' (Two Earner/Two or More Jobs) is the DEFAULT table for all employees; 'one_earner' (Optional One Earner/One Job: single, head of household, or married with non-employed spouse) is used only if the employee requests the lower rate on the IT-104.

income.formula: IT-100.2A (March 2026) percentage method: (1) Taxable wage = period gross wage - ($2,000/yr per IT-104 exemption, per-period equivalents above). (2) Apply the table for the period and the employee's table type, then round the result to the nearest whole dollar. Annual Two Earner (default): $0-$7,500: 2.11%; $7,500-$18,750: $158.25 + 2.81% over $7,500; $18,750-$30,000: $474.38 + 3.16% over $18,750; $30,000-$45,000: $829.88 + 4.22% over $30,000; over $45,000: $1,462.88 + 4.58% over $45,000. Annual Optional One Earner: $0-$10,000: 2.11%; $10,000-$25,000: $211.00 + 2.81% over $10,000; $25,000-$40,000: $632.50 + 3.16% over $25,000; $40,000-$60,000: $1,106.50 + 4.22% over $40,000; over $60,000: $1,950.50 + 4.58% over $60,000. Per-period tables are annual divided by periods with rounded breakpoints (e.g. biweekly two-earner $289/$722/$1,154/$1,731; biweekly one-earner $385/$962/$1,538/$2,308). (3) Add any additional amount requested on IT-104. Supplemental wages: annualize regular pay (pay per period x periods) and withhold on the supplemental payment at the marginal rate of the annual table that applies above that annual amount.
income.deviations: Fits the generic model (two selectable bracket tables, $2,000 per-exemption deduction) except: result is rounded to the nearest whole dollar, and per-period tables use rounded breakpoints. No flat supplemental rate (marginal-rate method described in formula).
income.localTaxes: No local income taxes. Several WV municipalities charge flat weekly 'city service' or 'user' fees that employers withhold from employees working inside city limits (amounts set by each city ordinance; SerieX does not calculate them).

sui.agency: WorkForce West Virginia, Unemployment Compensation Division
sui.notes: Wage base $9,500 under SB 841 (2024), effective July 1, 2024 (also 2025). New in-state employers 2.7%; new out-of-state construction employers 8.5% (includes 1% surtax). Experienced: positive-balance 1.5%-4.5%, negative-balance 6.5%-8.5% (includes 1% surtax). Confirm your rate with WorkForce West Virginia.

WV.deposit: Withheld tax is remitted on or before the 15th day of the following month; quarterly returns due by the last day of the month after the quarter. EFT required if prior-year liability exceeded $50,000. Employers withholding less than $600 a year (and certain household employers) file and pay annually by January 31. Employers filing for more than 10 employees, or using a payroll service, must file electronically (MyTaxes).
WV.quarterlyReport: Withholding: IT-101Q Employer's Quarterly Return of Income Tax Withheld (payments with IT-101V). UI: WVUC-A-154 Quarterly Contribution Report and WVUC-A-154-A Wage Report (WorkForce WV online system).
WV.annualReconciliation: WV/IT-103 Year End Reconciliation of withholding, with W-2s, due January 31
WV.notes: Mid-year change: SB 392 (signed March 31, 2026) cut all rates 5%, codified effective June 12, 2026 and retroactive to Jan 1, 2026 for the annual return. The Tax Division issued the March 2026 IT-100.2A/IT-100.2B tables; they apply to pay dates from June 12, 2026. Earlier 2026 pay dates (and all of 2025) used the 2025 tables: same breakpoints, rates 2.22%/2.96%/3.33%/4.44%/4.82% (two-earner annual bases $166.50/$499.50/$874.13/$1,540.13; one-earner $222.00/$666.00/$1,165.50/$2,053.50). Return-filing 2026 rates for married filing separately use half the thresholds ($5,000/$12,500/$20,000/$30,000). No state disability or paid leave program. SerieX uses the March 2026 tables (5% rate cut) for all 2026 paychecks. No flat supplemental rate.

WY.name: Wyoming

income.formula: No state individual income tax; no state withholding.

sui.agency: Wyoming Department of Workforce Services (DWS), Unemployment Insurance Division
sui.notes: Total rate = base rate + four adjustment factors (including the Employment Support Fund factor and the fund balance / non-charged factors), shown on the employer's rate notice. New employers (< 3 years) get a base rate equal to their industry's average (never below 1% before factors); experienced employers' base rate comes from their benefit ratio, statutory base-rate maximum 8.5% (also assigned if a report is filed before registration). DWS publishes no single minimum or maximum total rate for 2026, so they are not filled in; use the total rate on your rate notice. Wage base 2026 $33,800 (2025 $32,400; 2027 announced $34,900).

WY.deposit: No state income tax withholding. UI (and workers' comp) premiums paid quarterly with the quarterly report (due by the last day of the month after the quarter).
WY.quarterlyReport: Quarterly Summary Report for Unemployment Insurance and Workers' Compensation, filed via the WYUI portal
WY.notes: No state disability or paid leave program. 2027 UI wage base already published by DWS: $34,900. Unemployment rates are assigned to each employer, so the new employer, minimum and maximum rates are not filled in: enter the rate from your DWS rate notice in State settings.
